a26.speaker: A White House official (anonymous)
a26.name: A White House official (anonymous)
a26.speech: Claimed on July 3 that "President Trump believes that African countries offer incredible commercial opportunities which benefit both the American people and our African partners."

a26.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (on the US-Africa summit)
a26.name: Donald Trump
a26.title: US President (on the US-Africa summit)
a26.speech: Opened the summit claiming the five invited leaders were representing the entire African continent; thanked "these great leaders… all from very vibrant places with very valuable land, great minerals, great oil deposits, and wonderful people"; announced that the US was "shifting from AID to trade" because "this will be far more effective and sustainable and beneficial than anything else that we could be doing together."

a26.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (on Liberian President Boakai's English)
a26.name: Donald Trump
a26.title: US President (on Liberian President Boakai's English)
a26.speech: Marvelled at Joseph Boakai's "beautiful" English and asked, "Where did you learn to speak so beautifully? Where were you educated? Where? In Liberia?"

a26.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (on tariffs)
a26.name: Donald Trump
a26.title: US President (on tariffs)
a26.speech: Said he might not impose new tariffs on their countries "because they are friends of mine now."

a26.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (comment to journalist Hariana Veras)
a26.name: Donald Trump
a26.title: US President (comment to journalist Hariana Veras)
a26.speech: Told her, "You are beautiful – and you are beautiful inside."

a26.speaker: Mohamed Ould Ghazouani, President of Mauritania
a26.name: Mohamed Ould Ghazouani
a26.title: President of Mauritania
a26.speech: Praised Trump's "commitment" to Africa; described Trump as the world's top peacemaker, crediting him with stopping "the war between Iran and Israel."

a26.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a26.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a26.title: President of Senegal
a26.speech: Asked Trump to build a golf course in his country.

a26.speaker: Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, President of Gabon
a26.name: Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema
a26.title: President of Gabon
a26.speech: Talked of "win-win partnerships" with the US.

a263.speaker: Luísa Meque, chairperson of Mozambique’s National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a263.name: Luísa Meque
a263.title: chairperson of Mozambique’s National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a263.speech: Speaking on Tuesday in Maputo during the launch of the PEGDI, said over 800,000 people are displaced in the country, most affected by extreme violence carried out by Islamist terrorists in Cabo Delgado and by natural disasters: “We refer to the destruction of homes, where families have lost their possessions, some due to terrorism, others because they have suffered from the impacts of cyclones. Natural disasters have affected many families” ; “we hope to reduce the number of people at risk of displacement and create a favorable environment to find lasting solutions, through the provision of essential services during their return, local integration and integration elsewhere in the country” ; said the figures are worrying and there is a need to boost humanitarian assistance ; “This plan defines actions to respond to internal displacement and poverty reduction in terms of access to basic social services such as education, health, sanitation and water supply, social inclusion and security, as well as economic protection and opportunities” ; revealed that, during the peak of the terrorist attacks in Cabo Delgado, around 1.4 million people were displaced, of whom around 600,000 have already returned to their areas of origin.

a276.speaker: Seydou Asman, Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.name: Seydou Asman
a276.title: Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.speech: Recalls that, following the floods that occurred in the country and in order to allow citizens to rebuild their homes, the Head of State, Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, signed an ordinance setting the derogatory tax regime applicable to the import, production and marketing of CEM II 32.5 R grey cement, so that later, through a joint order signed between the Minister of Commerce and Industry and the Minister of Economy and Finance, the price per tonne of this type of cement could be fixed by region.

a276.speaker: Seydou Asman, Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.name: Seydou Asman
a276.title: Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.speech: Says that the cement companies sell cement only to their approved wholesalers and not to retailers, and that the fixed price per tonne included the wholesaler's profit margin, which he could share with his retailer ; "But we noted that the wholesalers do not want to share this margin per tonne with their retailers," so about ten days later a corrective meeting was held with the wholesalers, cement companies, retailers and transporters, after which all actors in the chain understood the need to comply with the government order; a memorandum of understanding on the transport of CEM II 32.5 R cement was signed between the Ministry, the Ministry of Transport and Equipment and the Collective of Transporters' Unions.

a276.speaker: Seydou Asman, Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.name: Seydou Asman
a276.title: Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.speech: Says that where non-compliance with the order was observed, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry deployed its sworn agents in the field: eight control teams criss-cross Niamey during the day and four more at night, working Monday to Sunday including public holidays; at the two entry points to Niamey, Sorey and Niamey 2000, two teams are permanently stationed in collaboration with Road Maintenance Fund (FER) agents and defence and security force agents, who take and hold the trucks' papers until delivery to the designated wholesaler, so the Ministry has daily control over the quantity of cement sold; the MCC plant at Malbaza and MANGO cement at Badaguichiri regularly send lists of trucks with registration number, tonnage, point of sale and the wholesaler to whom the truck is assigned.

a276.speaker: Seydou Asman, Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.name: Seydou Asman
a276.title: Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.speech: Says that when some resellers failed to respect the price, measures were taken to close thirteen (13) points of sale (wholesalers and retailers); besides the closure decision, each offender paid a fine of one million (1,000,000) FCFA to the State of Niger, paid directly to the Treasury by the Ministry's collector; others who had entered the cement trade seeking profit abandoned it of their own accord, so that today it can relatively be affirmed that the cement sales sector has been cleaned up.

a276.speaker: Seydou Asman, Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.name: Seydou Asman
a276.title: Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.speech: "First of all, something must be corrected, nobody carries out a commercial activity in order to operate at a loss." Says the price of a tonne ex-factory, the transport price and the wholesaler's profit margin are known, and it is on that basis that the Minister of Commerce and Industry and the Minister of Finance jointly fixed the price per tonne across the national territory; before the price reduction some wholesalers took 30 to 45 days to sell 10 tonnes of cement, but today cement sells out within a few hours whatever the quantity, and cement sellers earn between 90,000 and 100,000 FCFA profit per truck; "How, between us, can we speak of loss here?" Adds that the State made enormous sacrifices by giving up entirely all taxes, duties and other levies linked to the cement business, and that he is astonished that a handful of traders claim to make no profit, an attitude that testifies to a long-standing mercantilist spirit.

a276.speaker: Seydou Asman, Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.name: Seydou Asman
a276.title: Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.speech: Says the traders' cost calculation is a false calculation: the 10,000 FCFA municipal charge is 10,000 FCFA per truck and not per tonne; in Niamey, 45,000 FCFA per tonne ex-factory plus 8,000 FCFA transport gives 53,000 FCFA, with a 2,000 FCFA margin for the wholesaler making 55,000 FCFA, so the tonne can indeed be sold at 55,000 FCFA in Niamey; for a truck carrying 50 tonnes the municipal entry tax works out at no more than 200 FCFA per tonne, bringing the price to 53,200 FCFA. Says prices were fixed on that basis together with the cement companies, approved wholesalers, the Directorate General of Taxes (DGI) and the Directorate General of Customs (DGD), under the supervision of the Ministry, and that he is very pleased the question was asked so as to remove the ambiguity created by a tendentious interpretation that could mislead consumers and activists.

a276.speaker: Seydou Asman, Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.name: Seydou Asman
a276.title: Minister of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a276.speech: Says that tens of thousands of consumers request cement every day while Niger has only two cement production plants with limited capacity, creating a shortfall on the market because demand exceeds supply; there has never been a production stoppage nor a supply break, it is the number of people waiting for cement that has exploded; the Ministry draws up a national table of cement sold each day and reports to the relevant authorities daily, and control teams work Monday to Sunday and even on public holidays; invites consumers to go to the wholesale cement sellers who are ready to serve them according to available quantity and order of arrival ; "we reassure our fellow citizens that CEM II 32.5 R cement will continue to be produced and sold at the prices we have fixed" and, God willing, a third cement plant will be established at Tamaske in the coming months, in accordance with the mission letter entrusted to us by the Head of State and his firm commitment to industrialise Niger.

a276.speaker: Traders of the city of Niamey
a276.name: Traders of the city of Niamey
a276.speech: say the tonne of cement at the factory is sold at 45,000 FCFA, and adding the transport price of 8,000 FCFA, plus 10,000 FCFA to the municipality at the entrance to the city, plus unloading costs per tonne varying from 750 FCFA to 1,000 FCFA, they estimate the total at more than 60,000 francs for a tonne that must be resold at 55,000 francs on the market; these are the reasons they advance to explain the shortage of 32.5 cement in the city. Some claim that transporters are refusing this market since transport prices were fixed, complaining of operating at a loss.

a276.speaker: Some cement wholesalers
a276.name: Some cement wholesalers
a276.speech: certify that they have never achieved a turnover as large as since the adoption of this measure.

a286.speaker: General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, Sudan's de facto military leader
a286.name: General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan
a286.title: Sudan's de facto military leader
a286.speech: Said the talks taking place in Saudi Arabia with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) will have no benefit without a ceasefire ; "We can discuss a settlement after we reach a permanent ceasefire in Khartoum," he said in a live phone interview with AlQahera News, warning that war would spread to the rest of Sudan if a division happens in the capital Khartoum ; "The situation is stable in all states except for Khartoum" ; said earlier on Monday that the army was seeking a peaceful solution but that there could be discussions about a lasting settlement only "after we reach a permanent ceasefire in Khartoum".

a286.speaker: General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan
a286.name: General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan
a286.speech: Added that, to avoid being targeted by military forces, members of the "brutal and oppressive" RSF are "seeking shelter in civilian homes and in service centres".

a286.speaker: Insiders (anonymous)
a286.name: Insiders (anonymous)
a286.speech: Said discussions were not leaning towards a lasting ceasefire.

a286.speaker: Saudi diplomat (anonymous), speaking to AFP
a286.name: Saudi diplomat (anonymous)
a286.title: speaking to AFP
a286.speech: Told AFP news agency that the discussions have yielded "no major progress" ; "A permanent ceasefire isn't on the table ... both sides believe they are capable of winning the battle".

a286.speaker: The combatants (Sudanese army and RSF)
a286.name: The combatants (Sudanese army and RSF)
a286.speech: Have previously said they would try to tackle only a ceasefire and humanitarian issues like safe passage.

a286.speaker: Witnesses in Khartoum
a286.name: Witnesses in Khartoum
a286.speech: Said the sound of air strikes and clashes echoed anew across Khartoum on Monday.

a286.speaker: Hiba Morgan, Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Khartoum
a286.name: Hiba Morgan
a286.title: Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Khartoum
a286.speech: Said there has been intense fighting between the RSF and the Sudanese army ; "There were heavy air strikes launched by Sudanese army fighter jets ... around the vicinity of the presidential palace and in the central part of Khartoum" ; "Throughout the day we could see smoke rising from around that area as well as in east Nile where residents say air strikes were also launched by Sudanese army fighter jets" ; said there were also reports of artillery shelling in Khartoum North, and that residents who were there say it is likely the "surface-to-air missiles that are being fired by the RSF against the Sudanese army fighter jets".

a286.speaker: Doctors in Khartoum (via Al Jazeera's Hiba Morgan)
a286.name: Doctors in Khartoum (via Al Jazeera's Hiba Morgan)
a286.speech: Say the situation in hospitals around Khartoum is very dire, that they are running out of medicine, have a shortage of staff, and are in desperate need of assistance.

a286.speaker: Mahjoub Salah, a 28-year-old doctor in Khartoum
a286.name: Mahjoub Salah
a286.title: a 28-year-old doctor in Khartoum
a286.speech: Witnessed heavy fighting and a neighbour getting shot in the abdomen in his central Khartoum district of Al Amarat last month ; "We're still waiting for our passports to get issued, but we don't know how long this will take." ; "Then our plan is to travel from Port Sudan to Saudi Arabia."

a286.speaker: Saudi Foreign Ministry
a286.name: Saudi Foreign Ministry
a286.speech: Said "pre-negotiation" talks were "in the expectation of reaching an effective short-term ceasefire to facilitate humanitarian assistance".

a286.speaker: US Department of State
a286.name: US Department of State
a286.speech: Said it believed the sides had also discussed protecting civilians.

a286.speaker: Dafallah Alhaj, envoy to army chief al-Burhan
a286.name: Dafallah Alhaj
a286.title: envoy to army chief al-Burhan
a286.speech: "We are not for negotiation right now with [RSF chief] General Hemedti," said in South Sudan on Monday.

a286.speaker: Kholood Khair, director of Confluence Advisory, a Sudanese think-tank
a286.name: Kholood Khair
a286.title: director of Confluence Advisory, a Sudanese think-tank
a286.speech: "Key domestic and international stakeholders are not there like Egypt and the UAE, who are the only ones so far who have proven that they can guarantee a ceasefire" ; "That no civilians are present recreates failings of previous political negotiations," adding that African states that support civilian rule in Sudan were also not present.

a286.speaker: UN refugee agency (UNHCR)
a286.name: UN refugee agency (UNHCR)
a286.speech: Has registered more than 30 000 people crossing into South Sudan since the fighting erupted, more than 90 percent of them South Sudanese, and says the true number is likely much higher.

a501.speaker: King Mensah, Togolese music star
a501.name: King Mensah
a501.title: Togolese music star
a501.speech: Testified that he had received a great deal of support from the Beninese public in his musical rise in Africa. "I am an empty bag and it is you who have kept me standing since the beginning of my career," King Mensah declared on stage.

a501.speaker: King Mensah, Togolese music star
a501.name: King Mensah
a501.title: Togolese music star
a501.speech: Returned to the dream that is dear to his heart, helping orphaned children: "Even if I am not a billionaire, I believe that what I have will be enough to realise this dream that is dear to my heart," he said. He explained that he was only 13 when life took his father from him, and that having managed to make a name for himself despite many difficulties, he decided to help children in a similar situation to get ahead in life ; as founder of a humanitarian aid centre for children in Togo, he promises actions in favour of Benin's orphans.

a647.speaker: A local source (anonymous)
a647.name: A local source (anonymous)
a647.speech: Said the decision to halt fuel tanker traffic is intended to establish the destination or destinations of the fuel carried by these numerous tankers.

a647.speaker: Colonel-Major Olivier Diassana, Governor of the Bandiagara Region
a647.name: Colonel-Major Olivier Diassana
a647.title: Governor of the Bandiagara Region
a647.speech: explained that “this is by no means an arbitrary measure, but rather a strategy in the fight against the terrorism that is seriously affecting the Region” ; warned “against any form of complicity with armed groups” and called on the population to be vigilant and to cooperate with the security forces.

a647.speaker: Colonel-Major Olivier Diassana, Governor of the Bandiagara Region
a647.name: Colonel-Major Olivier Diassana
a647.title: Governor of the Bandiagara Region
a647.speech: On the subject of taxing phone top-ups and money transfers, explained that the measure is part of “a drive for economic sovereignty, as desired by the country’s highest authorities,” and insisted on the civic nature of this contribution, underlining that it will contribute to the socio-economic development of the nation ; called for a collective awakening to ensure the stability and development of the Bandiagara region.

a647.speaker: Koro Communal Youth Council (headed by Ousmane Edem Niangaly) and the civic forces of Koro (communique)
a647.name: Koro Communal Youth Council (headed by Ousmane Edem Niangaly) and the civic forces of Koro (communique)
a647.speech: issued a communique “to draw the attention of fuel dealers and resellers to the abusive increase in fuel prices in the town” ; “A price increase that further raises the cost of living and is considered a criminal act against a population already suffering from the effects of the security crisis.” ; the communique, signed by the village chief of Koro, the presidents of the Communal Youth Council, of civil society, of the local Chamber of Commerce, of the road hauliers, and by the president of the Coordination of Women’s Associations and Organisations (CAFO), specifies that “any person who takes it upon themselves to sell petrol at a price above the official price will be apprehended and brought before the competent authorities.”

a647.speaker: Service stations of Koro (some fifteen)
a647.name: Service stations of Koro (some fifteen)
a647.speech: declared that they were out of petrol, causing a shortage in the town.

a647.speaker: Representatives of traditional and religious authorities (Bandiagara)
a647.name: Representatives of traditional and religious authorities (Bandiagara)
a647.speech: reaffirmed their commitment to supporting these initiatives.

a742.speaker: TANAKA Akihiko, President, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a742.name: TANAKA Akihiko
a742.title: President, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a742.speech: Writes that as the 9th Tokyo International Conference on African Development (TICAD9) convenes in Yokohama, the conference arrives at a critical juncture amid intensifying global challenges such as climate change, geopolitical fragmentation, and economic inequality, and offers a vital platform to reimagine development cooperation rooted in mutual respect, innovation, and strategic partnership; argues that at the heart of this vision lies Africa's youth, since by 2050 one in four people globally will be African, a demographic dividend that can only be realized through sustained investment in education, healthcare, and job creation, without which the same demographic forces could deepen poverty and instability.

a742.speaker: TANAKA Akihiko, President, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a742.name: TANAKA Akihiko
a742.title: President, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a742.speech: Says Japan's ODA, led by JICA, has long championed the principle of "homegrown development," emphasising empowering local communities to create their own solutions rather than imposing external models, citing the Coalition for African Rice Development (CARD), which doubled rice production across the continent in a decade and now aims to double production again to 56 million tons by 2030, and initiatives like SHEP and KAIZEN which have empowered farmers and workers; says that underlying all of JICA's efforts is the concept of human security, a guiding principle reaffirmed in Japan's revised Development Cooperation Charter in 2023, meaning ensuring that individuals are free from fear and want and can live with dignity, a principle more relevant than ever in a world facing compounded crises.

a742.speaker: TANAKA Akihiko, President, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a742.name: TANAKA Akihiko
a742.title: President, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a742.speech: Says Africa's youth are not just beneficiaries but innovators, and that JICA launched Project NINJA (Next Innovation with Japan) in 2020, connecting African startups with Japanese investors and expertise, and in 2025 signed its first Grant Aid agreement with Nigeria to support local startups; announces that at TICAD9 JICA will unveil the IDEA (Impact Investing for Development of Emerging Africa) Initiative, designed to mobilize private capital for socio-economic development and climate action, complemented by the Japanese government's amendment of the JICA Act in April 2025 enabling JICA to take financial risks and catalyze private investment.

a742.speaker: TANAKA Akihiko, President, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a742.name: TANAKA Akihiko
a742.title: President, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a742.speech: Says human exchange is central to the Africa-Japan partnership, noting that since 2013 the ABE Initiative has enabled over 1,900 African students to study in Japan and intern with Japanese companies, and announcing that JICA will launch TOMONI Africa at TICAD9 to expand face-to-face exchanges between African and Japanese youth; cites the Japan-Africa Youth Camp of May 2025 and the work of over 16,000 Japanese Overseas Cooperation Volunteers in Africa since 1965, and JICA's partnerships with the AfCFTA Secretariat, Corridor Development, One Stop Border Posts, and triangular cooperation with countries like Egypt, Brazil and Indonesia.

a742.speaker: TANAKA Akihiko, President, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a742.name: TANAKA Akihiko
a742.title: President, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a742.speech: Concludes that Africa stands at a crossroads, with real challenges of poverty, conflict and governance but equally powerful opportunities in youth, innovation and resilience, and that for Japan, engaging with Africa is not charity, but a strategic investment in a shared future: "The future is not something to be given—it is something to be built, together."

a781.speaker: General staff of the Malian armed forces (etat-major general des armees)
a781.name: General staff of the Malian armed forces (etat-major general des armees)
a781.speech: The provisional toll communicated by the general staff reports five wounded soldiers, treated by the medical services, and twenty-one terrorists neutralised; a significant quantity of military equipment, communication equipment, vehicles and logistics was recovered in the locality.

a781.speaker: General staff of the Malian armed forces (etat-major general des armees)
a781.name: General staff of the Malian armed forces (etat-major general des armees)
a781.speech: Gave assurances that all measures will be taken to secure the area durably, protect civilians, facilitate free movement and prevent any attempt by armed groups to re-establish themselves in the region.

a781.speaker: General staff of the Malian armed forces (communique)
a781.name: General staff of the Malian armed forces (communique)
a781.speech: In its communique, paid tribute to the professionalism and courage of the soldiers engaged, while stressing that the struggle for the stabilisation of central and northern Mali requires constant and determined action.

a781.speaker: Testimonies gathered from reliable local sources (cross-checked by several Malian media outlets)
a781.name: Testimonies gathered from reliable local sources (cross-checked by several Malian media outlets)
a781.speech: Reported that living conditions in Sebabougou had become extremely precarious: supply cuts, movement restrictions, violence and constant threats.

a854.speaker: Xi Jinping, Chinese President
a854.name: Xi Jinping
a854.title: Chinese President
a854.speech: Put forward the principles of China's Africa policy – sincerity, real results, amity and good faith, and pursuing the greater good and shared interests, charting the course for China's cooperation with Africa, and providing the fundamental guidelines.

a854.speaker: Xi Jinping and African leaders, at the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) Beijing Summit
a854.name: Xi Jinping and African leaders
a854.title: at the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) Beijing Summit
a854.speech: Unanimously decided that the two sides would work to build an even stronger China-Africa community of shared future, advance cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative, establishing a new milestone in China-Africa relations.

a854.speaker: China and Africa at the FOCAC Beijing Summit 2018
a854.name: China and Africa at the FOCAC Beijing Summit 2018
a854.speech: Reached a strategic agreement to build a China-Africa community of shared future characterized by joint responsibility, win-win cooperation, happiness for all, cultural prosperity, common security, and harmony between humanity and nature.

a854.speaker: China (government)
a854.name: China (government)
a854.speech: Announced an exemption from debt incurred in the form of interest-free Chinese government loans due to mature by the end of 2018, applying to Africa's least developed countries, heavily indebted and poor countries, landlocked developing countries and small island developing countries that have diplomatic relations with China.

a854.speaker: China, at the China-Africa Internet Development and Cooperation Forum (August 2021)
a854.name: China
a854.title: at the China-Africa Internet Development and Cooperation Forum (August 2021)
a854.speech: Announced its intention to formulate and implement a joint China-Africa Partnership Plan on Digital Innovation in Africa.

a855.speaker: Court of the District of Sao Filipe (court record)
a855.name: Court of the District of Sao Filipe (court record)
a855.speech: Applied a ban on leaving the country and suspension of duties to three public servants from the island of Fogo, aged between 35 and 42, who are being investigated on suspicion of several crimes of embezzlement in continuous form and were detained outside of flagrante delicto in a case registered at the Public Prosecutor's Office of the District of Sao Filipe.

a855.speaker: Court of the District of Sao Filipe (court record)
a855.name: Court of the District of Sao Filipe (court record)
a855.speech: Ordered pretrial detention for an individual suspected of sexually abusing a five-year-old child.

a855.speaker: Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministerio Publico)
a855.name: Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministerio Publico)
a855.speech: Ordered the opening of an investigation to determine the circumstances of the death of a newborn girl during the evacuation process from Fogo to the city of Praia, over facts capable of constituting the crime of negligent homicide.

a1011.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC executive secretary
a1011.name: Elias Magosi
a1011.title: SADC executive secretary
a1011.speech: In a communique at the end of a one-day virtual SADC Extraordinary Summit of the Heads of State and Government in Harare on Thursday, said the regional body terminated the SAMIDRC mandate and directed the commencement of a phased withdrawal of SAMIDRC troops from the DRC.

a1011.speaker: SADC Extraordinary Summit of Heads of State and Government (communique)
a1011.name: SADC Extraordinary Summit of Heads of State and Government (communique)
a1011.speech: Noted the continued deterioration of the security situation in the Eastern DRC, including the capture of Goma and Bukavu, and the blockage of the main supply routes, making it difficult for humanitarian aid to flow; called for the protection and free movement of civilians seeking safety and for all parties to uphold international humanitarian principles, stop attacks on civilians' infrastructure, and guarantee unhindered humanitarian access ; "Summit noted the increasing humanitarian needs in the DRC and called on the international community, including the United Nations, and the African Union to provide humanitarian assistance to the people of the DRC" ; "Summit reiterated the need for a political and diplomatic solution with all parties including state, non-state parties, military and non-military in the Eastern DRC for the restoration of peace, security and tranquillity in the country." ; "Summit further reiterated the decision from the joint Summit of the East African Community (EAC) and SADC to merge the Luanda and Nairobi Processes and inclusion of more facilitators to enhance the peace-building process."

a1011.speaker: SADC leaders
a1011.name: SADC leaders
a1011.speech: Welcomed the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) 2773 Resolution which gives guidance for a long lasting solution while supporting the regional efforts by the AU, East African Community (EAC), Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS), International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR), and SADC, in convening high-level meetings and the efforts under the Luanda and Nairobi mediation processes, as well as the efforts by the United Nations Secretary-General to restore peace and security in Eastern DRC.

a1023.speaker: National Trade Facilitation Committee (CNFC) of Mozambique
a1023.name: National Trade Facilitation Committee (CNFC) of Mozambique
a1023.speech: Announced today in Maputo the end of the issuance of manual phytosanitary certificates, which will henceforth be issued in electronic format as part of trade facilitation and digitalisation; the decision was taken during a meeting that also reviewed the activity report for the period 2018 to 2024.

a1023.speaker: Claire Zimba, National Director of External Trade
a1023.name: Claire Zimba
a1023.title: National Director of External Trade
a1023.speech: Explained that, as this was the first session, the report presenting the main results was analysed ; "We made a significant assessment of the simplified trade regime that Mozambique has agreed and is now implementing with Malawi. You know that today at the borders micro-operators can carry out transactions of up to one thousand dollars a day, a much more simplified procedure" ; "We also reviewed, in this first session of the steering committee, the launch of what is finally the process of digitalising phytosanitary certificates" ; "The information was given with much joy that the electronic certificate has already been launched, which means that manual phytosanitary certificates are no longer issued; this is important because when wanting to export, in the case of an agricultural product there is always a need to issue a sanitary certificate" ; said that at the meeting held on Friday the parties reviewed the start-up of one-stop border posts under the agreement established between Mozambique and Malawi, with four borders selected, two of which will shortly begin operating as a pilot phase.

a1094.speaker: Hu Bin, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Djibouti
a1094.name: Hu Bin
a1094.title: Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Djibouti
a1094.speech: Said the Conference was held at the moment when the 20th anniversary of the Forum's creation is being celebrated, and was also the first ministerial Conference of the Forum since the first China-Arab States Summit at the end of 2022, contributing greatly to accelerating the implementation of the achievements of the first 2022 Summit and the building of a China-Arab community of shared future oriented towards the new era.

a1094.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China
a1094.name: Xi Jinping
a1094.title: President of China
a1094.speech: Delivered a speech at the opening ceremony of the Conference, retracing the long-standing friendship between China and the Arab countries and outlining the fine prospects of their relations in the new era ; said the friendship uniting China and the Chinese people with the Arab countries and peoples has its source in friendly exchanges along the ancient Silk Roads, in the common struggle for national liberation and in win-win cooperation for the development of their countries ; stressed China's constant willingness to work with its Arab friends so that China-Arab relations set an example in preserving world peace and stability, in high-quality cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative, in harmonious coexistence between different civilisations and in exploring the right path of global governance ; proposed the "joint construction of five cooperation architectures", namely a more dynamic architecture for innovation, a broader architecture for investment and financial cooperation, a more multidimensional architecture for energy cooperation, a more balanced architecture for mutually beneficial economic and trade exchanges, and a vaster architecture for human and cultural exchanges.

a1094.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1094.name: Wang Yi
a1094.title: Chinese Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1094.speech: In his address proposed working on four priorities: further strengthening mutual strategic trust and firmly supporting one another on respective vital interests; further deepening pragmatic cooperation and promoting higher-level win-win cooperation; further strengthening coordination at the international level to jointly maintain the right course of global governance; and further strengthening the building of the Forum to contribute to the fine prospects of the China-Arab community of shared future ; said China intends to work with its Arab brothers and sisters to make the spirit of China-Arab friendship shine, marked by mutual assistance, solidarity, equality, shared benefit, inclusiveness and mutual inspiration, and to consolidate the Forum's cooperation mechanisms to achieve more fruitful China-Arab collective cooperation for the next 20 years.

a1094.speaker: Arab participants at the Conference
a1094.name: Arab participants at the Conference
a1094.speech: In their interventions, highly appreciated the fruits obtained within the Forum over the past 20 years, especially the notable progress achieved in implementing the achievements of the first 2022 Summit; said they were encouraged by the ideas proposed by President Xi on the future development of China-Arab relations and the "joint construction of five cooperation architectures", which they said will give strong impetus to establishing a new type of China-Arab partnership; and underlined their wish to work with China to further strengthen Arab-Chinese strategic coordination and accelerate implementation of the achievements of the first 2022 China-Arab Summit and of the Conference.

a1094.speaker: Hu Bin, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Djibouti
a1094.name: Hu Bin
a1094.title: Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Djibouti
a1094.speech: Said it was a meeting that valorised the achievements obtained, fostered unity and cooperation and opened new prospects for the future; that its high point was the participation of President Xi, King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa of Bahrain, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Al Sissi, Tunisian President Kaïs Saïed and UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in the opening ceremony; that its most important result was President Xi's announcement that, echoing the resolution of the Arab League summit of heads of State, the second China-Arab Summit would be held in China in 2026; and that the strongest voice heard was that of firm support for the restoration of the legitimate national rights of the Palestinian people, calling for a rapid end to the conflict in Gaza and a comprehensive, just and lasting settlement of the Palestinian question.

a1094.speaker: Beijing Declaration (Conference document)
a1094.name: Beijing Declaration (Conference document)
a1094.speech: Reviews the important consensus reached at the first 2022 China-Arab Summit and the progress made in implementing its achievements, and clarifies the path to follow to promote the building of a China-Arab community of shared future; reiterates that China and the Arab States will continue to support each other on questions of vital interest and to deepen their win-win cooperation; and reaffirms their common positions on the political settlement of regional questions, dialogue between civilisations, global governance, counter-terrorism, human rights and artificial intelligence, climate change, etc.

a1094.speaker: 2024-2026 Cooperation Implementation Plan (Conference document)
a1094.name: 2024-2026 Cooperation Implementation Plan (Conference document)
a1094.speech: Provides for the strengthening of the Forum's mechanisms and of multilateral and bilateral cooperation in various fields such as politics, economy and trade, investment, finance, infrastructure, resources and the environment, human and cultural exchanges, aeronautics and aerospace, education and health.

a1094.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China
a1094.name: Xi Jinping
a1094.title: President of China
a1094.speech: On the Palestinian question, affirmed that since last October the Palestinian-Israeli conflict had escalated brutally, causing deep suffering to local populations; said that the war must not last indefinitely, that justice must not be eternally absent, and above all that the two-State solution must not be arbitrarily called into question; stressed that consequently China firmly supports the creation of an independent and fully sovereign Palestinian State on the basis of the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital, supports Palestine's accession to the UN as a full member and supports the holding of an international peace conference of greater scope, greater authority and more substance.

a1094.speaker: China-Arab Joint Declaration on the Palestinian Question (Conference document)
a1094.name: China-Arab Joint Declaration on the Palestinian Question (Conference document)
a1094.speech: Expresses their deep common concern in the face of the humanitarian crisis caused by the prolonged conflict in Gaza and reaffirms their firm attitude and unshakeable consensus on a ceasefire in Gaza, the guarantee of humanitarian aid, opposition to the forced displacement of the Palestinian people, support for Palestine's accession to the UN, and a rapid settlement of the Palestinian question on the basis of the two-State solution.

a1094.speaker: Hu Bin, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Djibouti
a1094.name: Hu Bin
a1094.title: Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Djibouti
a1094.speech: Said Djibouti has always been an active participant in and contributor to China-Arab collective cooperation and made important contributions to the success of the Conference, for which China expresses its high appreciation and sincere thanks; said China is willing to work with Djibouti and other members of the China-Arab Forum to accelerate implementation of the achievements of the first 2022 Summit and of the Conference and to launch preparations for the second 2026 Summit, with the aim of achieving deeper strategic mutual trust, better-quality mutually beneficial cooperation and a higher level of inclusiveness and mutual inspiration; and said China intends to work with its Djiboutian brothers and sisters to strengthen the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC), especially to make a great success of the 2024 FOCAC Summit, to illustrate the excellence of the China-Djibouti strategic partnership and bring greater benefits to the two peoples.

a1194.speaker: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) (statement signed by Hakama Sidi-Ali, Acting Director of Corporate Communications)
a1194.name: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) (statement signed by Hakama Sidi-Ali
a1194.title: Acting Director of Corporate Communications)
a1194.speech: Dismissed reports suggesting distress in a regulated financial institution, describing the claims as misleading and capable of triggering unnecessary panic in the financial system, and assured Nigerians that the country's banking sector remains "resilient, safe, and sound." "The CBN wishes to categorically reassure the public, depositors, and stakeholders that the Nigerian banking sector remains resilient, safe, and sound." ; "All licensed banks are subjected to stringent regulatory requirements. There is no cause for concern regarding the safety of depositors' funds."

a1194.speaker: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) (statement)
a1194.name: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) (statement)
a1194.speech: Noted that it maintains a robust risk-based supervisory framework and early warning systems to detect and address vulnerabilities before they escalate. "The Bank affirms that it continues to monitor all financial institutions under its regulatory purview and maintains robust frameworks for early warning signals and risk-based supervision." ; "These mechanisms ensure that any emerging issues are promptly addressed to protect the integrity of the financial system."

a1194.speaker: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)
a1194.name: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)
a1194.speech: Urged the public to disregard unverified claims circulating online and instead rely on official communication channels for accurate updates about Nigeria's financial system; the statement reiterated the CBN's commitment to "fostering a secure banking environment where depositors can be fully confident in the safety of their funds."

a1220.speaker: John Charuk S. Siafa, Monrovia City Mayor
a1220.name: John Charuk S. Siafa
a1220.title: Monrovia City Mayor
a1220.speech: Making the disclosure at a press briefing in Monrovia, without outlining the types of misbehaviours, revealed that after investigating several of the complaints, several officers were found culpable and have since been suspended. He further disclosed that the suspended officers are expected to face prosecution in the coming days. "Those officers who were found guilty of misconduct have been suspended, and we are preparing to turn their cases over to the court for prosecution."

a1220.speaker: John Charuk S. Siafa, Monrovia City Mayor
a1220.name: John Charuk S. Siafa
a1220.title: Monrovia City Mayor
a1220.speech: Emphasized that while many officers continue to serve with dedication, the city administration will not tolerate any form of corruption within its ranks. He assured the public that disciplinary measures will be taken swiftly whenever credible complaints are brought forward. "While we recognize the hard work of many officers in maintaining order, we will not tolerate any misconduct. We are committed to acting when complaints arise." ; "We applaud the good work done by many in the City Police, but we will not hesitate to act against those who tarnish the institution's image." ; "The public deserves transparency, and we remain open to addressing any concerns raised by citizens."

a1494.speaker: African Centre for Credible Leadership (ACCL) (statement signed by its President, Dr. Ifure A. Ifure)
a1494.name: African Centre for Credible Leadership (ACCL) (statement signed by its President
a1494.title: Dr. Ifure A. Ifure)
a1494.speech: Has commended the Dangote Refinery for its groundbreaking impact on Nigeria’s fuel subsidy regime and its recent reduction in fuel prices. “The African Centre for Credible Leadership (ACCL) wishes to commend the Dangote Refinery for its groundbreaking impact on Nigeria’s fuel subsidy regime and its recent reduction in fuel prices,” the statement said. “The refinery’s operationalization has significantly altered the narrative on fuel subsidy, paving the way for a more sustainable and self-sufficient energy ecosystem. We acknowledge the visionary leadership of Aliko Dangote, whose commitment to investing in Africa’s growth has yielded a game-changing project. The Dangote Refinery’s contribution to Nigeria’s energy landscape attests to the power of private sector-driven initiatives in transforming the continent’s economic fortunes.”

a1494.speaker: Dr. Ifure A. Ifure, President of the African Centre for Credible Leadership (ACCL)
a1494.name: Dr. Ifure A. Ifure
a1494.title: President of the African Centre for Credible Leadership (ACCL)
a1494.speech: Noted that the recent reduction in fuel prices, which saw the ex-depot price of petrol slashed from N970 to N899 per litre, is expected to bring relief to Nigerians across the country: “The recent reduction in fuel prices is a welcome development that will bring relief to Nigerians across the country. By slashing the ex-depot price of petrol from N970 to N899 per litre, Dangote Petroleum Refinery has demonstrated its commitment to supporting the Nigerian government’s efforts to stabilize the economy.” ; Ifure said the reduction in fuel prices is expected to have a positive impact on the economy, boosting productivity, reducing business costs, and helping to revive the economy: “The reduction in fuel prices is not just about saving money at the pump; it is about boosting productivity, reducing business costs, and helping to revive the economy. When fuel costs go down, it impacts everything from the delivery of goods to the pricing of services. Transporters, farmers, and small businesses all stand to benefit from this reduction, which could lead to lower overhead costs and increased economic activity.”

a1494.speaker: African Centre for Credible Leadership (ACCL)
a1494.name: African Centre for Credible Leadership (ACCL)
a1494.speech: Praised Dangote’s partnership with MRS Oil Nigeria Plc to offer petrol at N935 per litre across all MRS filling stations nationwide, describing it as a bold step towards addressing the long-standing issue of price disparities across states: “This move will ensure that every Nigerian has access to affordable fuel, regardless of their geographical location.”

a1494.speaker: African Centre for Credible Leadership (ACCL)
a1494.name: African Centre for Credible Leadership (ACCL)
a1494.speech: Also commended Dangote’s commitment to corporate social responsibility and his support for the Nigerian government’s economic revival efforts, and urged other African business leaders and governments to draw inspiration from the Dangote Refinery’s success story and replicate similar initiatives that can drive economic growth, reduce dependence on foreign aid, and improve the lives of African citizens.

a1712.speaker: Bertha Bangara Chikadza, President of the Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a1712.name: Bertha Bangara Chikadza
a1712.title: President of the Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a1712.speech: Says Malawi was supposed to be assisted to rebuild its foreign exchange reserves and provided with enough financing to build productive sectors to attain macroeconomic stability. In a written response, she said Malawi could not rebuild its international reserves when it is not producing enough amid collapsing exports and could not curb inflation amid food shortages that came with cyclones and El Nino; she said Malawi could also not restructure its external debt, currently at around $4.27 billion (about K7.5 trillion) because the lenders needed to agree to debt restructuring, which means losing their profits. "However, as a country, we should not wait for the IMF to have fiscal discipline or have sustainable revenue mobilisation to improve public financial management and reduce domestic borrowing, which is a key ingredient to achieving debt sustainability and supporting appropriate monetary policy to contain money growth and curb inflation." ; She said while losing some of the aid might impact the country negatively and affect its aspirations, Ecama "sees this as a decisive act of wanting to have thorough discussions with the IMF on the conditions that come with ECF."

a1712.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, Scotland-based Malawian economist
a1712.name: Velli Nyirongo
a1712.title: Scotland-based Malawian economist
a1712.speech: Said the major concern has been lack of fiscal discipline and clear policy direction, with monetary and fiscal policies often misaligned and government spending exceeding budgeted limits. He observed that although bilateral partners have provided some assistance, the absence of a comprehensive agreement with all creditors has hampered the country's ability to achieve meaningful debt relief. "Furthermore, austerity measures and structural reforms have often faced resistance due to their adverse impact on the population, particularly the most vulnerable groups."

a1712.speaker: Betchani Tchereni, Secretary to the Treasury
a1712.name: Betchani Tchereni
a1712.title: Secretary to the Treasury
a1712.speech: Said in a statement on Wednesday evening that the programme faced a number of exogenous (external) shocks, which made it difficult for the supply side to assist both increased revenue and enhanced production.

a1712.speaker: Treasury source (anonymous)
a1712.name: Treasury source (anonymous)
a1712.speech: Noted that government was required to reduce fiscal deficits annually, but on the contrary, it contributed with an expansionary fiscal stance soon after the ECF was approved. "The kwacha realignment against major currencies was designed to reduce the pressures on kwacha as people were rushing for foreign imports, but this too did not happen just as was the case with the need to restructure non-performing institutions such as Export Development Fund."

a1712.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a1712.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a1712.speech: Has given Malawi key policy recommendations to help restore macroeconomic stability, including strengthening fiscal discipline and sustainability, rebuilding of international reserves and facilitating an exchange rate regime that supports external stability, restructuring external commercial debt to support debt sustainability, and structural reforms to improve governance and unleash productivity to support growth.

a1890.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopian Prime Minister
a1890.name: Abiy Ahmed
a1890.title: Ethiopian Prime Minister
a1890.speech: Led the ceremony in Calub, unveiling what he called a landmark in Ethiopia's industrial transformation ; “This is a cornerstone of our economic independence — supporting agriculture, energy security, and technological advancement,” Abiy said.

a1890.speaker: Officials (unnamed)
a1890.name: Officials (unnamed)
a1890.speech: Say the Calub complex will supply up to 1,000 megawatts of power to Ethiopia's national grid and emerging high-demand industries such as data centers and cryptocurrency mining, and that it will also serve as feedstock for fertilizer and petrochemical plants.

a1890.speaker: Energy analysts (unnamed)
a1890.name: Energy analysts (unnamed)
a1890.speech: Say the new direction reflects Ethiopia's push for import substitution and industrial diversification, aligning with its “Homegrown Economic Reform” blueprint.

a1890.speaker: Observers (unnamed)
a1890.name: Observers (unnamed)
a1890.speech: Caution that key operational details remain undisclosed, including final production capacity, financing arrangements, and environmental safeguards. Without greater transparency, they warn, the project's long-term impact may remain uncertain despite its symbolic significance.

a1980.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (statement)
a1980.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (statement)
a1980.speech: Expressed its surprise following an announcement made on social media by the United States Department of Government Efficiency on 15 February 2025, and informed the public that it had officially contacted the American authorities about these recent allegations; according to the statement signed by Abdoulaye Diop, the matter concerns an alleged grant of 14 million US dollars, equivalent to about 8 billion 800 million CFA francs, intended to support social cohesion.

a1980.speaker: United States Department of Government Efficiency (social media post, 15 February 2025)
a1980.name: United States Department of Government Efficiency (social media post
a1980.title: 15 February 2025)
a1980.speech: Listed Mali among the countries whose American grants had been cancelled.

a1980.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1980.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a1980.title: Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a1980.speech: Recalled that, in its quest to preserve its sovereignty, Mali has regularly denounced the misuse of development aid as a potentially destabilising instrument ; stressed that the financing of terrorist networks and the violation of the sovereignty of States were major concerns, even before the installation of the new American administration.

a1980.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (statement)
a1980.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (statement)
a1980.speech: Affirmed that Mali appreciates the new approach of the American authorities, who aim to clean up and humanise their grants, and welcomes this awareness regarding the reality of their public aid as well as the steps taken to counter its subversive use, which did not meet the fundamental needs of the beneficiaries ; calls on the American authorities to prosecute those who diverted these funds to finance international terrorism, of which Mali and the other States of the AES Confederation are victims.

a1980.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (statement)
a1980.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (statement)
a1980.speech: Reaffirmed that the Malian authorities, faithful to the values that underpin their public action, will continue their efforts to guarantee security, restore peace, promote social cohesion and foster sustainable development, within a framework of national ownership, partnership, mutual respect, and in the context of the Confederation of Sahel States.

a1995.speaker: Tedros Adhanom, Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)
a1995.name: Tedros Adhanom
a1995.title: Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)
a1995.speech: argued that peace is the best medicine for the problems of the African continent and stated that conflicts are an obstacle to the development of the continent; considered that there needs to be investment in people for the continent to develop: “The choices we make now will shape the future of global health financing and we need to get it right. Because, ultimately, health is not a cost to be contained. It is an investment to be nurtured, an investment in people, in stability and in economic growth. But there is one thing even more fundamental to Africa’s future than health. And I join you in this, my brother Mo, and that one thing is peace. The best way to achieve peace is to have the best medicine: peace. Without peace, nothing else will make a difference.”

a1995.speaker: Tedros Adhanom, Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)
a1995.name: Tedros Adhanom
a1995.title: Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)
a1995.speech: admitted that the sudden cuts to foreign aid by Western countries are affecting the distribution of medicines, the payment of health professionals and the financing of other infrastructure, and said the difference between crisis and opportunity is everyone’s leadership: “First, now is the moment for the leadership of governments to free themselves from the yoke of aid dependency and to chart the path to self-sufficiency. Second, we need the leadership of creditors in the form of concessional loans on fair terms. When African countries pay more to borrow than high-income countries, there is something wrong with the system. And third, we need the leadership of generous donors, not to pay salaries and operating costs of health or other programmes, but to develop the capacity so that we can run them ourselves.” ; said the WHO is working to help African countries become more efficient and self-sufficient in the face of the reduction in foreign aid, a challenge the organisation itself faces.

a2063.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a2063.name: John Dramani Mahama
a2063.title: President of Ghana
a2063.speech: Rallied the nation to support his agenda to reset the country and help it break free from its cycle of dependence on foreign aid, stating that proclaiming self-reliance while relying on donors was meaningless: “Proclaiming self-reliance while marching straight back into the hands of the donor agencies, begging bowl in hand, is really meaningless. To break this cycle of dependence and reset our economy, my administration is formulating policies based on fiscal discipline and living within our means to expand our economy to yield prosperity for all” ; “We must look within and make sure that we are raising revenue domestically” ; said discussions about Ghanaians' independence often highlighted reliance on imports, donor aid, and IMF bailouts as signs of continued dependence: “Yet the entire efficacy of this reminder lies not in just repeating it but in our willingness to take decisive action.”

a2063.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a2063.name: John Dramani Mahama
a2063.title: President of Ghana
a2063.speech: Said his administration was working to implement a 24-hour economy programme to ensure that the economy never went to sleep, which would create job expansion, boost productivity, increase exports capacity and trade footprints and reduce dependence on foreign aid; said the $10 billion Big Push initiative would modernise infrastructure, create jobs, stimulate local industry and ensure development was driven from within rather than funded from outside, and that agriculture remained “our biggest opportunity to reduce import dependence”; named the Agriculture for Economic Transformation agenda, the Feed Ghana programme and the Poultry Farm to Table (Nkukor Nkete Nkete) initiative as policies to strengthen local agribusiness, ensure food security and address the 95 per cent reliance on imported poultry products ; stressed that success would depend on active citizen participation, particularly from young people: “My brothers and sisters, this is a defining moment, but policies alone, no matter how well couched and no matter how well intentioned, will not change our reality. Action will change that reality” ; pledged to take the necessary actions to create growth opportunities and enhance economic independence and entreated young Ghanaians to step up to the plate.

a2063.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a2063.name: John Dramani Mahama
a2063.title: President of Ghana
a2063.speech: Reflected on Ghana's progress since independence and said the celebration was a reminder of the nation's struggles for freedom and self-rule: “It reinforces our national identity, our unity and patriotism while offering a moment for reflection on our progress and the challenges ahead” ; added that it would have been “unconscionable” to spend GH¢20 million on the Independence Day celebration as was done in the past: “This is necessary considering the economic crisis our nation is currently experiencing. Large-scale celebrations often come with significant security and infrastructure costs, which strain the national budget” ; “By reducing the scale of the commitment, we wish to demonstrate a commitment to fiscal responsibility and the efficient use of our limited resources.”

a2063.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a2063.name: John Dramani Mahama
a2063.title: President of Ghana
a2063.speech: Recalled Ghana's history, saying Dr Kwame Nkrumah envisioned “an industrialised, self-reliant Ghana whose citizens had the highest standard of economic life and the greatest sense of self-esteem rooted in patriotism and Pan-African unity”; emphasised that “the verdict of history is now loud and clear” on his overthrow on February 24, 1966; said “these independence anniversaries must therefore be a moment of reflection, not on what we have done for ourselves but on how well we have stewarded national assets for those we will hand them over to in the future” ; called on Ghanaians to strive for more, saying “Our story cannot be one of missed opportunities; it will be one of continued efforts to achieve far more than we can boast of now”, and warned that “posterity will not accept our failures or take them kindly.”

a2067.speaker: Save the Children (UK-based global charity)
a2067.name: Save the Children (UK-based global charity)
a2067.speech: Revealed last month's deaths on Wednesday, saying they were among the first directly linked to cuts ordered by US President Donald Trump, who slashed funding for global health programmes under his "America First" policy after taking office on January 20.

a2067.speaker: Christopher Nyamandi, Save the Children's country director in South Sudan
a2067.name: Christopher Nyamandi
a2067.title: Save the Children's country director in South Sudan
a2067.speech: "There should be global moral outrage that the decisions made by powerful people in other countries have led to child deaths in just a matter of weeks."

a2067.speaker: Experts
a2067.name: Experts
a2067.speech: Have warned that the funding cuts - including the cancellation of more than 90 percent of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) contracts - could lead to millions of deaths from malnutrition, AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria in the years ahead.

a2067.speaker: US State Department
a2067.name: US State Department
a2067.speech: Said it had no information about the reported deaths.

a2067.speaker: US State Department spokesperson (anonymous, cited by Reuters)
a2067.name: US State Department spokesperson (anonymous
a2067.title: cited by Reuters)
a2067.speech: Insisted that many US-funded humanitarian projects in South Sudan remained operational but accused the country's leadership of misusing foreign aid: "While emergency lifesaving programmes continue, we will not, in good conscience, ask the American taxpayer to provide assistance that effectively subsidises the irresponsible and corrupt behaviour of South Sudan's political leaders."

a2067.speaker: South Sudan's government
a2067.name: South Sudan's government
a2067.speech: Has admitted to widespread corruption but denies specific allegations of graft, including against President Salva Kiir's family.

a2067.speaker: The United Nations
a2067.name: The United Nations
a2067.speech: Has warned that fighting in the northeast could push the country towards a new civil war.

a2067.speaker: UN Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a2067.name: UN Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a2067.speech: According to UNICEF, about 40,000 cholera cases and 700 deaths were recorded between September and March after an outbreak was declared in October last year ; about half of those stricken by the disease are children under 15.

a2094.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2094.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2094.speech: Warns against disruptions to health services: these are already being reported in 70% of its country offices surveyed following the sudden suspensions and reductions of Official Development Assistance earmarked for health.

a2094.speaker: WHO stocktake/survey of 108 WHO country offices, March-April 2025 (report)
a2094.name: WHO stocktake/survey of 108 WHO country offices
a2094.title: March-April 2025 (report)
a2094.speech: Shows that many countries are striving to increase or reallocate funding from domestic and other external sources to make up for funding losses; up to 24% of responses suggest the budget cuts are already translating into an increase in direct out-of-pocket payments by patients; suspensions and reductions of ODA are disrupting all health system functions, the most frequently reported affected areas being health emergency preparedness and response (70%), public health surveillance (66%), service delivery (58%), humanitarian aid (56%) and the health and care workforce (54%); health services are disrupted across all areas in at least one third of responding countries; the nature and scale of disruptions are in some contexts comparable to those observed during the acute phases of the COVID-19 pandemic; one third of countries surveyed are without essential commodities for major services; the pause in ODA has led to job losses for health and care workers in more than half of responding countries; in more than 40% of countries key information systems have been disrupted; 81 of the 108 WHO country offices expressed the need for support in a wide range of health-related areas, including innovative financing and resource mobilisation and targeted technical assistance.

a2094.speaker: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the WHO
a2094.name: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a2094.title: Director-General of the WHO
a2094.speech: "These findings paint a worrying picture of the impact of sudden and unplanned cuts in aid on the health of millions of people," he lamented. "While representing a shock, these cuts are also pushing an accelerated transition from dependence on aid towards a more sustainable self-reliance based on domestic resources. Many countries are asking for WHO's support, and the Organization is working with them to identify and adapt the most effective measures."

a2094.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2094.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2094.speech: Given the rapidly evolving context, the WHO stated that it will regularly monitor the situation and mobilise the global health community, including its partners and donor agencies, in order to design emergency response plans aimed at mitigating the worsening repercussions on countries and enabling greater long-term viability.

a2410.speaker: Independent UN experts (four special rapporteurs and members of the Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances, mandated by the UN Human Rights Council)
a2410.name: Independent UN experts (four special rapporteurs and members of the Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances
a2410.title: mandated by the UN Human Rights Council)
a2410.speech: Denounced the endangerment of migrants and refugees in Tunisia during rescue operations at sea or transfers to border areas, in a report commissioned by the UN Human Rights Council ; "We have received shocking reports of dangerous maneuvers during operations to intercept migrants, refugees and asylum seekers at sea," citing in particular beatings and the capsizing of boats ; noted that between January and July, 189 people, including children, reportedly lost their lives during the crossings and 265 during interception operations at sea, while 95 people are missing ; "For those who are 'rescued' by the coast guard, including victims of trafficking, their situation would only worsen upon disembarkation in the ports."

a2410.speaker: Independent UN experts (four special rapporteurs and members of the Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances)
a2410.name: Independent UN experts (four special rapporteurs and members of the Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances)
a2410.speech: Reported allegations of arbitrary forced transfers to the borders with Algeria and Libya, without humanitarian assistance ; "We are dismayed by the reported violence and the excessive use of force during these transfers. Migrants, refugees and asylum seekers, including children and pregnant women, are reportedly taken to desert areas on the border with Algeria and Libya, and border guards would shoot at them if they tried to come back."

a2410.speaker: Independent UN experts (statement/communique)
a2410.name: Independent UN experts (statement/communique)
a2410.speech: Expressed concern at reports that sub-Saharan migrants, refugees and asylum seekers "are subjected to higher levels of violence by Tunisian security forces", at the crackdown on civil society organisations and human rights defenders which has led to the temporary suspension of pre-registration activities and limited migrants' access to basic services, and at the increase in the number of criminal groups involved in human trafficking and reports of sexual violence, including the rape of women and girls as young as ten in the border areas.

a2410.speaker: Independent UN experts (concluding statement)
a2410.name: Independent UN experts (concluding statement)
a2410.speech: "We are concerned that, despite these serious allegations, Tunisia continues to be considered a safe place after search and rescue operations at sea, and that cooperation continues (...) between the European Union and Tunisia."

a2475.speaker: Central Bank of Liberia (CBL)
a2475.name: Central Bank of Liberia (CBL)
a2475.speech: Has attributed the recent rise in the exchange rate to the high demand for foreign currency during the Christmas season, saying the surge was driven by increased spending on imports for holiday-related purchases during the festive season: "Any time Christmas passes, we will experience an increased exchange rate because of these economic factors" ; reassures that these exchange rate spikes are recurring and steps are being taken to address their long-term impact.

a2475.speaker: Jerolinmek Mathew Piah, Liberian Information Minister (speaking on behalf of the Central Bank)
a2475.name: Jerolinmek Mathew Piah
a2475.title: Liberian Information Minister (speaking on behalf of the Central Bank)
a2475.speech: "What is happening is normal and temporary. The rate will adjust. This is happening because people spent more money during Christmas to buy goods in U.S. dollars, which increases the demand for foreign currency, putting pressure on the exchange rate."

a2475.speaker: Jerolinmek Mathew Piah, Liberian Information Minister
a2475.name: Jerolinmek Mathew Piah
a2475.title: Liberian Information Minister
a2475.speech: Revealed that as of November 2024, the amount of Liberian dollars in circulation accounted for less than four percent of the country's nominal GDP and less than 15 percent of the total money supply; also said that the net U.S. dollar remittance for goods at the end of November 2024 was estimated at $661.8 million; and said the low proportion of Liberian dollars in circulation limits its influence on the overall economy and exchange rate fluctuations.

a2475.speaker: Jerolinmek Mathew Piah, Liberian Information Minister
a2475.name: Jerolinmek Mathew Piah
a2475.title: Liberian Information Minister
a2475.speech: Assured the public that the government is working to address these challenges and that the rate will readjust; encouraged citizens to invest in the Central Bank's bills, which he claims offer an attractive 17 percent interest rate; "The CBL remains committed to collaborating with the community and other stakeholders to closely monitor the foreign exchange market and ensure stable macroeconomic development."

a2475.speaker: Government of Liberia
a2475.name: Government of Liberia
a2475.speech: Urges the public to desist from speculative behavior in the foreign exchange market, so the economy can maintain its stability.

a2511.speaker: Prof Sharon Lewin, director of the Doherty Institute and past president of the International Aids Society
a2511.name: Prof Sharon Lewin
a2511.title: director of the Doherty Institute and past president of the International Aids Society
a2511.speech: Says the world should this year have been "talking about the virtual elimination of HIV" in the near future: "Within five years. Now that's all very uncertain." ; says there is a risk of "dramatic increases in infections, dramatic increases in death and a real loss of decades of advances."

a2511.speaker: Prof Sharon Lewin, director of the Doherty Institute and past president of the International Aids Society
a2511.name: Prof Sharon Lewin
a2511.title: director of the Doherty Institute and past president of the International Aids Society
a2511.speech: Says access to drugs represents an "immediate crisis": "If people with HIV stop the medications, then not only do they get sick themselves, which is tragic, but they also then become infectious to others."

a2511.speaker: Prof Sharon Lewin, director of the Doherty Institute and past president of the International Aids Society
a2511.name: Prof Sharon Lewin
a2511.title: director of the Doherty Institute and past president of the International Aids Society
a2511.speech: Says the mood at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections in San Francisco was "dire"; says that as well as programme cancellations, there are "huge concerns around science and what's going to happen to the [US] National Institutes of Health, [whose] funding of science has been so significant on every level"; says some scientists in receipt of US funding have been told to remove their names from DEI-linked research, even though DEI is fundamental to the HIV response: "I don't mean that in a sort of touchy-feely way, I mean that's what we need to do: you need to actually get those treatments to these diverse communities."

a2511.speaker: UNAids (surveillance)
a2511.name: UNAids (surveillance)
a2511.speech: Doctors, nurses and other healthcare workers have been laid off, while worried patients are hoarding drugs or stretching supplies, according to UNAids surveillance.

a2511.speaker: Elizabeth Glaser Paediatric Aids Foundation
a2511.name: Elizabeth Glaser Paediatric Aids Foundation
a2511.speech: Says it has had to halt HIV treatment for 85,000 people in Eswatini, including more than 2,000 children, and tests for thousands of pregnant women and babies to prevent transmission and begin life-saving medication.

a2511.speaker: Gilead (manufacturer of lenacapavir)
a2511.name: Gilead (manufacturer of lenacapavir)
a2511.speech: New results from the manufacturer Gilead suggest that a tweak to the formula and how it is given could see the protective effects of lenacapavir last even longer.

a2511.speaker: Prof Linda-Gail Bekker, of South Africa's Desmond Tutu Health Foundation
a2511.name: Prof Linda-Gail Bekker
a2511.title: of South Africa's Desmond Tutu Health Foundation
a2511.speech: Says she has seen US funding for three trials of potential HIV vaccines involving eight countries cancelled and only reinstated after an appeal to the US supreme court: "We're running around like chickens without heads to at least get one going, because the vaccines are sitting in the fridge and will expire."

a2511.speaker: Prof Linda-Gail Bekker, of South Africa's Desmond Tutu Health Foundation
a2511.name: Prof Linda-Gail Bekker
a2511.title: of South Africa's Desmond Tutu Health Foundation
a2511.speech: Worries about HIV/Aids prevention "falling off the radar completely"; says the global community had been making headway towards the United Nations' goal of ending Aids by 2030 with a five-year plan to use "amazing new innovative tools and scale them up", which would have led to "less dependence on foreign aid and more self-reliance": "All of that is hugely at risk now because, without these funds, our governments will have to step up but they will concentrate on treatment. We know they will do that, because that is what we did for the first 30 years." ; says efforts to control Aids were entering "the last mile", which was always likely to be more expensive: "The people who were happy to come into health facilities, they would have come into health facilities." ; says it would be difficult to rely on government funding to reach the remaining groups, not only because of fewer resources but also because in some countries it means targeting groups whose existence is illegal and unrecognised; "I feel like the odds are very stacked against us," adding: "We're obviously going to have to re-programme ourselves [and] formulate a different plan."

a2511.speaker: Prof Linda-Gail Bekker, of South Africa's Desmond Tutu Health Foundation
a2511.name: Prof Linda-Gail Bekker
a2511.title: of South Africa's Desmond Tutu Health Foundation
a2511.speech: Fears the Global Fund might receive fewer than the planned number of lenacapavir doses: "Six months ago, I was saying the best thing we can do with lenacapavir is offer it to everybody in a choice environment. [Now] I think we're gonna have to say who needs [injectable] prep, and the rest have to do the best they can. How do we make that decision? And what does that look like? It is back to sort of rationing." ; "When we started ARVs [antiretroviral drugs] way back in 2000, you would go, 'you get treatment; you don't, you don't, you don't'."

a2511.speaker: Global Fund to Fight Aids, Tuberculosis and Malaria
a2511.name: Global Fund to Fight Aids
a2511.title: Tuberculosis and Malaria
a2511.speech: Has promised to maintain its commitment to deploy lenacapavir doses in low-income countries.

a2575.speaker: Western critics' letter (European statement on Tanzania)
a2575.name: Western critics' letter (European statement on Tanzania)
a2575.speech: raises allegations about supposed abductions and calls for the release of political figures, as though the country's own legal institutions were incapable of addressing complex cases in line with due process; purports to "express concern" over democracy in an African country.

a2575.speaker: Julius Nyerere, founding President of Tanzania
a2575.name: Julius Nyerere
a2575.title: founding President of Tanzania
a2575.speech: He warned that true independence would mean little if Africans merely exchanged colonial governors for foreign advisers. "We must think for ourselves," he said, "and govern ourselves in our own way." ; "No one has the right to tell other people how to organize their society."

a2575.speaker: Andrew Mwenda, journalist
a2575.name: Andrew Mwenda
a2575.title: journalist
a2575.speech: once said that the West's biggest export to Africa is its moral arrogance, the belief that every African problem is caused by the West not acting quickly enough.

a2720.speaker: Aliko Dangote, President/Chief Executive of Dangote Group
a2720.name: Aliko Dangote
a2720.title: President/Chief Executive of Dangote Group
