a2720.speech: described it as "a game changer" and "an important achievement for our country as it demonstrates our ability to develop and deliver large capital projects"; said the statement answered the curiosity of Nigerians on when it will be in the market, adding that it will be in Nigeria's oil market before the end of January once it receives regulatory approval.

a2720.speaker: Dangote Group (statement)
a2720.name: Dangote Group (statement)
a2720.speech: said the refinery has so far received six million barrels of crude oil at its two single-point moorings located 25km from the shore, that the first crude delivery was done on December 12, 2023, and the sixth cargo was delivered on January 8, 2024. "The refinery can load 2,900 trucks a day at its truck-loading gantries, and the products will conform to Euro V specifications. The refinery design complies with the World Bank, US EPA, European emission norms, and the country's oil regulator's emission/effluent norms, employing state-of-the-art technology."

a2739.speaker: Black Hills (utility company)
a2739.name: Black Hills (utility company)
a2739.speech: Said on Tuesday it would buy peer NorthWestern Energy for $3.6 billion, creating a larger regulated utility with greater scale to invest in grid infrastructure and meet rising energy demand.

a2739.speaker: Reuters (calculation)
a2739.name: Reuters (calculation)
a2739.speech: According to Reuters calculation, the all-stock deal implies a per-share value of about $59, a premium of 7.66% to NorthWestern’s last close.

a2739.speaker: Brian Bird, NorthWestern Energy CEO
a2739.name: Brian Bird
a2739.title: NorthWestern Energy CEO
a2739.speech: “Together, we will be better positioned to meet rising demand, accelerate investment in energy and grid infrastructure, and support customers and communities through a rapidly evolving energy landscape.”

a2757.speaker: White House National Security Council
a2757.name: White House National Security Council
a2757.speech: Told Today News Africa in November the criteria for inviting African governments to attend the U.S.-Africa Leaders Summit scheduled for December 13-15; in a statement, said four countries were not invited because they are suspended by the African Union following military coups and counter coups - Burkina Faso, Guinea, Sudan, and Mali.

a2757.speaker: Biden Administration (statement)
a2757.name: Biden Administration (statement)
a2757.speech: The summit "will demonstrate the United States enduring commitment to Africa, and will underscore the importance of U.S.-Africa relations and increased cooperation on shared global priorities. Africa will shape the future - not just the future of the African people, but of the world. Africa will make the difference in tackling the most urgent challenges and seizing the opportunities we all face."

a2757.speaker: Washington (U.S. government)
a2757.name: Washington (U.S. government)
a2757.speech: Says the summit will focus on existing challenges, especially those relating to peace and security, food security, climate change and poverty alleviation directions across Africa.

a2757.speaker: Dana Banks, White House Senior Director for Africa
a2757.name: Dana Banks
a2757.title: White House Senior Director for Africa
a2757.speech: Said the White House administration has been pushing for the Prosper Africa Build Together Campaign that would drive billions of dollars of investment in Africa.

a2757.speaker: Linda Thomas-Greenfield, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations
a2757.name: Linda Thomas-Greenfield
a2757.title: U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations
a2757.speech: Said the long-planned trip is not part of global competition with either of America's rivals, but is part of a series of high-level U.S. engagements "that aim to affirm and strengthen our partnerships and relationships with African leaders and peoples." ; "We're not catching up. They are catching up. We have been engaging with this continent for decades, and even my own career is very much evidence of that."

a2757.speaker: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (statement)
a2757.name: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (statement)
a2757.speech: Announced that the foundation will spend $7 billion over the next four years to improve health, gender equality and agriculture across Africa, and that it will further continue to invest in researchers, entrepreneurs, innovators and healthcare workers working to unlock the human potential that exists across the continent, noting that the Russia-Ukraine crisis was reducing the amount of aid flowing to the continent and created global instability; it appeals to global leaders to step up their commitments to finding solutions to multiple problems in African countries.

a2757.speaker: Summit for Democracy (December 2021, Biden administration description)
a2757.name: Summit for Democracy (December 2021
a2757.title: Biden administration description)
a2757.speech: Brought together leaders from government, civil society, and the private sector in a shared effort to set forth "an affirmative agenda for democratic renewal and to tackle the greatest threats faced by democracies today through collective action."

a2757.speaker: Antony J. Blinken, U.S. Secretary of State / new U.S. strategy for Africa (document)
a2757.name: Antony J. Blinken
a2757.title: U.S. Secretary of State / new U.S. strategy for Africa (document)
a2757.speech: Unveiled the new U.S. policy for Africa in South Africa in August, saying the United States will pursue four main objectives in Africa: fostering openness and open societies, delivering democratic and security dividends, advancing pandemic recovery and economic opportunities, and supporting conservation, climate adaptation and a just energy transition; the strategy begins by acknowledging that "Sub-Saharan Africa plays a critical role in advancing global priorities to the benefit of Africans and Americans," and that it "has one of the world's fastest growing populations, largest free trade areas, most diverse ecosystems, and one of the largest regional voting groups in the United Nations (UN)." For democracy and security dividends, the United States will focus on "working with allies and regional partners to stem the recent tide of authoritarianism and military takeovers, backing civil society, empowering marginalized groups, centering the voices of women and youth, and defending free and fair elections, improving the capacity of African partners to advance regional stability and security and reducing the threat from terrorist groups to the United States Homeland, persons, and diplomatic and military facilities."

a2757.speaker: Times Higher Education index
a2757.name: Times Higher Education index
a2757.speech: Indicated that approximately 43,000 Africans have currently enrolled into and are studying in American universities.

a2757.speaker: Joao Lourenco, Angolan President
a2757.name: Joao Lourenco
a2757.title: Angolan President
a2757.speech: In an interview with Hariana Veras, White House correspondent, praised President Joseph R. Biden Jr. for hosting the U.S.-Africa Leaders' Summit, saying that it will help create a win-win partnership between the United States and Africa, accelerate industrialization, increase direct foreign investment and further cement the already good collaboration between Angola and the United States; pointed to the assertiveness of the Biden administration's focus on trade and investment in Africa, highlighting America's commitment to Africa's security, its democratic development and its people.

a2757.speaker: Joao Lourenco, Angolan President
a2757.name: Joao Lourenco
a2757.title: Angolan President
a2757.speech: Advised that the Russian and Ukraine war should open the eyes of advanced countries to lead efforts in increasing investment in more alternative energy sources besides the traditionally used energy sources, and called for increased food production and investment in African nations, saying that the global food crisis has badly affected Africa.

a2834.speaker: Jean-Claude Houssou, Minister of Energy of Benin
a2834.name: Jean-Claude Houssou
a2834.title: Minister of Energy of Benin
a2834.speech: "The MCA-Benin II programme must truly transform Benin's energy sector." ; observed that the second compact is a major asset for the energy sector, to be used wisely, explaining that the agreement specifies the responsibilities incumbent on each party and that the SBEE must work tirelessly to achieve the objectives.

a2834.speaker: Christopher Broughton, resident director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2834.name: Christopher Broughton
a2834.title: resident director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2834.speech: said this agreement falls within the framework of the grant between the MCC and the government of Benin: "In accordance with this agreement, the SBEE has been identified as the implementing structure of Benin's second programme for the Millennium Challenge Account II." ; suggested that the SBEE's collaboration is indispensable to successfully carry out this programme.

a2834.speaker: Gabriel Degbegni, national coordinator of MCA-Benin II
a2834.name: Gabriel Degbegni
a2834.title: national coordinator of MCA-Benin II
a2834.speech: explained that in carrying out the programme's activities, MCA-Benin II will establish formal cooperative relations with various public and semi-public entities, which are partner structures indispensable to achieving the set objectives, and that besides the SBEE, MCA II will also sign agreements with the Electricity Regulatory Authority, the General Directorate of Energy, the Beninese Agency for Rural Electrification and Energy Management, the Electric Community of Benin, the Beninese Environment Agency and the town halls of the programme's intervention zones: "The implementation agreement therefore appears as a partnership contract between MCA-Benin II and these structures, in order to clearly define the obligations of each of the parties" ; stressed that it will strengthen the SBEE's capacities and make the projects' gains sustainable ; "I would like to count on the determination of each of the actors concerned for compliance with the obligations contained in this agreement."

a2899.speaker: Akawak Roba, CEO of Ethiopian Shipping Lines
a2899.name: Akawak Roba
a2899.title: CEO of Ethiopian Shipping Lines
a2899.speech: Through this courtesy visit, DMP's partners conveyed a message of congratulations to the Director General of the Doraleh Multipurpose Port, Mr. Djama Ibrahim Darar, and to all the teams who worked for the smooth running of port logistics and transport operations; Mr. Roba particularly congratulated all DMP staff, who spared no effort in handling a volume of 1,500,000 metric tonnes of dry bulk in record time.

a3026.speaker: TSA, Algerian media outlet
a3026.name: TSA
a3026.title: Algerian media outlet
a3026.speech: Reported on Monday that the government has directed private schools to stop accepting financial or other support from France.

a3026.speaker: Algeria's authorities
a3026.name: Algeria's authorities
a3026.speech: Argued that just as Algerian schools cannot teach their curriculum abroad without agreements, foreign curriculums shouldn't be taught in Algeria's schools unless officially approved.

a3026.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a3026.name: Emmanuel Macron
a3026.title: French President
a3026.speech: Shifted France's position by recognising Morocco's autonomy plan for Western Sahara as the “only basis” for resolving the conflict.

a3152.speaker: Fitch Ratings
a3152.name: Fitch Ratings
a3152.speech: Said on Thursday that pressure from U.S. aid freezes and global trade tension is unlikely to result in widescale credit downgrades in Africa ; said the impact of tariffs on Africa is limited due to the region’s export composition and weaker integration into global supply chains compared to a region such as Asia.

a3152.speaker: Fitch Ratings
a3152.name: Fitch Ratings
a3152.speech: Said the freeze on U.S. foreign aid was not without negative consequences: some of the poorest nations were at risk for having projects come to an abrupt end and would see fiscal stability come under pressure; Ethiopia received U.S. assistance worth around 80% of its foreign exchange reserves, with Mozambique, Uganda, and Lesotho also seen at risk.

a3152.speaker: Paul Gamble, head of Middle East/Africa in Fitch’s Sovereign Ratings Group
a3152.name: Paul Gamble
a3152.title: head of Middle East/Africa in Fitch’s Sovereign Ratings Group
a3152.speech: Said South Africa, Namibia and Ivory Coast remain relatively shielded from recent events, and told a webinar that Nigeria and the Seychelles both hold positive credit outlooks from Fitch Ratings thanks to ongoing reforms ; “The reforms that we’ve seen really put the region in a better position to absorb some of these shocks.” ; “The impact for the ratings looks manageable.”

a3152.speaker: Paul Gamble, head of Middle East/Africa in Fitch’s Sovereign Ratings Group
a3152.name: Paul Gamble
a3152.title: head of Middle East/Africa in Fitch’s Sovereign Ratings Group
a3152.speech: Pointed to Washington’s pivot to strategic investments in minerals in Africa as potentially becoming a new sphere for the trade tensions as it could intensify competition on the continent with China ; “Africa will be a playing field for U.S.-China tensions” ; said the U.S. interest is becoming “more opportunistic, transactional,” focusing on access to minerals and rare earths rather than broad-based development.

a3152.speaker: Arnaud Louis, senior director at Fitch
a3152.name: Arnaud Louis
a3152.title: senior director at Fitch
a3152.speech: “African-owned multilateral banks might become more important institutions in this shifting landscape,” said on the webinar.

a3152.speaker: Trump administration
a3152.name: Trump administration
a3152.speech: Has said it wants to invest billions of dollars in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

a3292.speaker: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a3292.name: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a3292.speech: Has reassured Nigerians, particularly Persons Living With HIV (PLWHIV), that the country has a steady supply of antiretroviral drugs and that HIV treatment services remain uninterrupted.

a3292.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General of NACA
a3292.name: Temitope Ilori
a3292.title: Director-General of NACA
a3292.speech: In a statement issued on Wednesday, noted that the federal government has taken proactive measures to prevent any disruption in HIV treatment services and emphasised that the government has recently made some key financial commitments to cushion the impact of the US government’s aid pause and close the immediate funding gap: “The Federal Executive Council (FEC) approved $1.07 Billion to finance the healthcare sector reforms under the Human Capital Opportunities for Prosperity and Equity (HOPE) programme, and also approved N4.8 billion for HIV treatment, while the Nigerian Senate also recently allocated an additional N300 billion to the health sector in the 2025 budget.” ; “These allocations are part of the government’s efforts to cushion the impact of the US government’s aid pause and close the immediate funding gap.” ; “We want to assure Nigerians, particularly those living with HIV, that there is no shortage of drugs and consumables and no immediate stop of services for HIV treatment, testing, and prevention in Nigeria.” She said all treatment centres and pharmacies will continue to have sufficient antiretroviral drugs, ensuring uninterrupted access to care.

a3292.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General of NACA
a3292.name: Temitope Ilori
a3292.title: Director-General of NACA
a3292.speech: While acknowledging the US government’s and its partners’ significant contributions over the past two decades, said Nigeria views this funding gap as an opportunity to take ownership of its HIV response and strengthen local solutions. She added that this is a crucial moment for the country to mobilise resources and ensure the sustainability of its HIV programme, reaffirmed NACA’s commitment to achieving HIV epidemic control in Nigeria and encouraged the public to rely on credible sources for updates regarding the country’s HIV response.

a3292.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a3292.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a3292.speech: Raised concerns that Nigeria and seven other countries could face shortages of life-saving HIV medication due to the United States’ pause on foreign aid ; had warned that disruptions caused by the US foreign aid suspension could reverse two decades of progress in the global fight against HIV, potentially leading to over 10 million new HIV infections and three million related deaths globally ; also warned that countries such as Haiti, Kenya, Lesotho, South Sudan, Burkina Faso, Mali, Nigeria, and Ukraine could face HIV drug shortages.

a3531.speaker: Bernie Sanders, former left-wing candidate in the 2016 US presidential election
a3531.name: Bernie Sanders
a3531.title: former left-wing candidate in the 2016 US presidential election
a3531.speech: In a speech in Denver, Colorado in March 2025 on the theme “fighting oligarchy” before more than 90,000 listeners: “The American people, especially with Mr Musk and the 13 billionaires in the Trump administration running agency after agency… Having travelled the country, I can tell you that the American people are fed up with this inequality and want an economy that benefits everyone, and not just the richest 1%… The richest 1% of our country now owns more wealth than the poorest 90%. CEOs earn 300 times more than their average employee. And as incredible as it may seem — given actual current inflation — the average American worker, despite a massive increase in productivity, is today lower than 52 years ago. And during that period, 75 trillion dollars of wealth have been transferred from the poorest 90% to the richest 1%... three Wall Street firms — BlackRock, Vanguard and State Street — are, together, the principal shareholders of 95% of our companies… the worst form of addiction this country currently faces is the greed of the oligarchy.”

a3531.speaker: Bernie Sanders, former left-wing candidate in the 2016 US presidential election
a3531.name: Bernie Sanders
a3531.title: former left-wing candidate in the 2016 US presidential election
a3531.speech: “And in that other America, 60% of our population lives paycheck to paycheck. And millions of workers from one end of the country to the other are trying to survive on miserable wages… Unlike Donald Trump, I grew up in a family that lived paycheck to paycheck… All over the country, rents are soaring… In the worst case, do I live in my car? Let us be clear. Many people who work today live in the back of their car… I challenge anyone in this country — let alone an elderly person, who needs health care, who needs to heat their home — to try to survive on 15,000 dollars a year… In my state, the cost of health care is rising by 10 to 15%. In the United States today, 85 million people are uninsured or under-insured… our health system has the function of generating billions of dollars of profits for the insurance companies and the pharmaceutical laboratories… We are the richest country in the world: 800,000 people sleep in the street and 20 million people spend more than 50% of their meagre incomes on housing.”

a3531.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3531.name: Donald Trump
a3531.title: US President
a3531.speech: His thunderous announcements of the elimination of USAID subsidies and of generalised sanctions to impose US hegemony, notably against South Africa for having taken measures of relative land redistribution driving a wedge into agrarian apartheid.

a3531.speaker: Samuel P. Huntington
a3531.name: Samuel P. Huntington
a3531.speech: “American multiculturalists reject their country’s cultural heritage. They [...] wish to create a country of many civilisations, that is to say a country belonging to no civilisation and devoid of cultural unity. History teaches us that no state thus constituted has ever endured as a coherent society.”

a3531.speaker: Collectif CartograFreeSenegal (data)
a3531.name: Collectif CartograFreeSenegal (data)
a3531.speech: Of the 65 deaths recorded by the Collectif CartograFreeSenegal during the battle against the outlaw APR/BBY state, 81% were by gunfire, and 46.5% of the dead were mechanic workers, 27.5% pupils and students and 12% traders, probably from the informal sector.

a3565.speaker: Adam Ibrahim, Sudanese aid worker with the UN humanitarian agency OCHA (former refugee)
a3565.name: Adam Ibrahim
a3565.title: Sudanese aid worker with the UN humanitarian agency OCHA (former refugee)
a3565.speech: “I was at home helping my daughter revise for her grade six exams, scheduled for the next day. Then, out of nowhere, the sound of heavy gunfire shattered the silence in my hometown, Zalingei, the capital of Central Darfur state, which remains gripped by insecurity and critical shortages of basic services. At first, I thought the gunfire would pass quickly. I rushed to stock up on food supplies and water, enough for six days. But, the streets became battlegrounds. All I could do was try to keep my family safe.” ; “Despite the chaos, I continued to work. Electricity and Internet access were sporadic, but I kept my phone charged to send daily updates to the OCHA Head of Office. It gave me purpose amid the uncertainty. Eventually, it became too dangerous to stay.” ; “On the 39th day, we fled. Our family of 10 began a harrowing journey with no clear destination, only the desperate need to escape. We left behind more than just walls and belongings; we left behind a life built with love and hope. Our journey took us first to Nyala in South Darfur, then to Kosti in White Nile State. From there, we crossed the border into neighbouring South Sudan and eventually reached Uganda... The journey by car took 23 days. My children had no passports, and there were no refugee camps for Sudanese nationals at the time.” ; “In Kampala, we rented a house and received asylum status within three days. The moment I held our refugee cards, I exhaled deeply and thought ‘we’ve made it.’” ; “Here I was, an aid worker now a refugee, needing the same support I once provided to others.”

a3565.speaker: Adam Ibrahim, Sudanese aid worker with the UN humanitarian agency OCHA (former refugee)
a3565.name: Adam Ibrahim
a3565.title: Sudanese aid worker with the UN humanitarian agency OCHA (former refugee)
a3565.speech: “Months later, I faced a difficult decision. Do I stay with my family or return to Darfur and continue the work I had done for years? I chose to return. Leaving my family behind was incredibly hard, but their safety was paramount.” ; “When I arrived in Zalingei, I barely recognised it. Buildings were scarred with bullet holes. I found another family sheltering inside our house, a doctor and his family whose own home had been destroyed... The house had been looted. Windows were gone and our belongings had vanished.” ; “Everyone was armed, even children as young as 15. People were tense, traumatised and always bracing for the next wave of violence.” ; “El Geneina’s streets were strewn with the wreckage of burned-out military vehicles. Armed men patrolled in pickup trucks mounted with machine guns. The humanitarian needs were immense. People lacked food, shelter, household essentials, healthcare, clean water and protection, but we never had enough resources for them.”

a3565.speaker: Adam Ibrahim, Sudanese aid worker with the UN humanitarian agency OCHA (former refugee)
a3565.name: Adam Ibrahim
a3565.title: Sudanese aid worker with the UN humanitarian agency OCHA (former refugee)
a3565.speech: “It’s heartbreaking to witness the suffering caused by the recent donor funding cuts. Many organizations have been forced to scale back their operations, leaving countless people without help. Still, we did all we could. Between 2023 and 2025, we reached more than 800,000 displaced people with critical assistance, in West and Central Darfur.” ; “Today, I remain in Sudan. My family is still in Uganda. I visit them once a year, but the separation is painful.”

a3565.speaker: 2025 Sudan humanitarian needs and response plan (UN funding data)
a3565.name: 2025 Sudan humanitarian needs and response plan (UN funding data)
a3565.speech: Cited as showing that more than 30.4 million people – over half Sudan's population – urgently need humanitarian assistance, yet the plan is severely underfunded, with only 13.3 per cent of the required resources received so far.

a3733.speaker: Franck Lokonon, National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.name: Franck Lokonon
a3733.title: National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.speech: “My name is Franck Lokonon, National Technical Director of volleyball of Benin.” ; “The presence of the National Technical Directorate (DTN) at this championship is really essential because the nursery at the volleyball level must be seen and maintained. Consequently, the DTN has made it its mission to support the government's projects by accompanying this schools championship.”

a3733.speaker: Franck Lokonon, National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.name: Franck Lokonon
a3733.title: National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.speech: On the level of play of the pupils: “In terms of play, I can tell you that the children have a very high level. The game rests on techniques that are executed, for some, to perfection, and for others, there is still work to be done. But I tell you, over the two years of the schools championship we have had in volleyball, the coaches have really made our children progress and we, as technicians, are happy about it. We get goosebumps at some matches where we see little children who give their all and who execute the set, the dig, the reception with a game intelligence that makes grown-ups want to come and watch volleyball matches.”

a3733.speaker: Franck Lokonon, National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.name: Franck Lokonon
a3733.title: National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.speech: On collaboration with the international experts recruited by the State: “The collaboration is going very well between the experts and the National Technical Directorate because the National Technical Directorate has its branches, which are the regional technical advisers, and who work hand in hand with the experts on all the selections, all the training camps... I can tell you that the boost that the presence of these experts gives us today in volleyball is not negligible. We should encourage it and do everything to get the best out of these experts so that after their departure from Benin... their generation will be a generation that will shine internationally.”

a3733.speaker: Franck Lokonon, National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.name: Franck Lokonon
a3733.title: National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.speech: On the value of the schools championships for the federations: “For the federations, you are not unaware that all sport rests on schools. And when these pupils grow up, they will come into civilian life. And we, the Federation, will have the pleasure of welcoming them. We will make it our duty to maintain them so that our federations truly live, because without the grassroots training we are doing, there will be no summit. In 10-15 years, those who are currently there will give way to those we are now seeing play very young today.”

a3733.speaker: Franck Lokonon, National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.name: Franck Lokonon
a3733.title: National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.speech: On the national championship: “I can tell you that we are currently at the 13th round of the championship and these are the return matches. We are heading towards the end of these return-phase matches in order to move to the grouped phase of the best and the less good so as to continue the second phase of our championship. And I assure you, at these grouped phases, you will again see volleyball and real volley.”

a3733.speaker: Franck Lokonon, National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.name: Franck Lokonon
a3733.title: National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.speech: On the export of players abroad: “We will thank our federation president who does everything to make our volleyball shine internationally. I want to name Mr Ali Yaro who really does a lot internationally to make our volleyball shine because he has those connections that allow others to come and see our championship and to come and take those who can validly represent us. We have exported more than one, we have partnerships with others and we assure you that these little ones we are discovering today will go through there.”

a3733.speaker: Franck Lokonon, National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.name: Franck Lokonon
a3733.title: National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.speech: On Queen's VBC's withdrawal from the Champions League: “I can tell you that the Queen's VBC team could not take part in the Zone 3 competition in Burkina Faso because the team is being rebuilt... At a certain point, the team saw that it would not be able to validly represent the country with the squad it currently has and it was able to decide not to participate. But I assure you, this team will always come back in force. I also thank the Energie VBC team which made a very strong impression in this Zone 3 Africa Cup championship, which is crowned with a silver medal... In two or three years, do not be surprised to see us in gold at the regional level.”

a3733.speaker: Franck Lokonon, National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.name: Franck Lokonon
a3733.title: National Technical Director (DTN) of the Beninese Volleyball Federation (FBVB)
a3733.speech: Concluding word: “I would sincerely thank all the journalists who work for the visibility of our sport, all those who, in the shadows, work so that sport can be seen internationally. I would thank all the officials of the National Technical Directorate who do everything to go and reach the smallest children in the furthest corners of Benin to make talents of them. I would also thank Mr President Ali Yaro for everything he does for Beninese volleyball. I will not forget the ministry which thought to place at the disposal of the sports federations technical officials, seasoned officials, for the reconstitution of Beninese sport. Thank you.”

a3737.speaker: Max Tonela, Mozambique's Minister of Economy and Finance
a3737.name: Max Tonela
a3737.title: Mozambique's Minister of Economy and Finance
a3737.speech: Invited to explain on a debate panel the reason behind the success of the government's policies, explained that the executive's openness to cooperating with the private sector was one of the most important factors in the expansion of the electricity grid in the country.

a3747.speaker: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) data
a3747.name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) data
a3747.speech: According to OECD data, sub-Saharan Africa absorbed nearly 40% of USAID's annual budget, with countries such as Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, Senegal and Nigeria among the main beneficiaries.

a3747.speaker: The White House
a3747.name: The White House
a3747.speech: According to the White House, USAID's missions will henceforth be integrated directly into a Directorate-General for Cooperation and Development attached to the US State Department; officially the aim is to streamline the structure, limit administrative duplication and strengthen the alignment between development aid and US diplomatic priorities.

a3747.speaker: World Bank
a3747.name: World Bank
a3747.speech: Recalls that the agency was among the top five bilateral donors for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) related to health, education and gender equality.

a3747.speaker: Government Accountability Office (GAO) report
a3747.name: Government Accountability Office (GAO) report
a3747.speech: Underlines that USAID managed more than 1,300 projects across 80 overseas missions, with occasional duplication between federal agencies.

a3747.speaker: US administration
a3747.name: US administration
a3747.speech: Defends a refocusing on major diplomatic priorities, in a context of heightened rivalry with China over investments in Africa and Asia; the dissolution is presented as a measure of sound management of public funds.

a3747.speaker: Several US officials
a3747.name: Several US officials
a3747.speech: Find that USAID's strength lay precisely in its operational autonomy and technical expertise; according to them, the technical expertise accumulated over decades by USAID teams could be diluted, even lost, within a broader diplomatic framework where aid risks becoming a mere instrument of geopolitical influence.

a3747.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa
a3747.name: Claver Gatete
a3747.title: Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa
a3747.speech: Stated recently at the eleventh session of the Africa Regional Forum on Sustainable Development held in Kampala, Uganda: “Aid can no longer be considered a reliable or sustainable solution. Time is pressing. We must act now, with you, our heads of state, who are leading reforms, creating an enabling environment and mobilising domestic resources. Together, we can deliver on the promise of Agenda 2063 and the SDGs.”

a3747.speaker: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, statistician-economist, specialist in economic policy management
a3747.name: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi
a3747.title: statistician-economist, specialist in economic policy management
a3747.speech: “Efforts must be made to diversify sources of financing by turning to regional and international financial markets and to innovative financing. The most predictable and most sustainable resources are domestic public resources.”

a3887.speaker: 2024/25 Livelihood and Vulnerability Assessment, conducted by the Office of the Prime Minister (Namibia)
a3887.name: 2024/25 Livelihood and Vulnerability Assessment
a3887.title: conducted by the Office of the Prime Minister (Namibia)
a3887.speech: According to the assessment, around 1.2 million Namibians of all ages are currently affected by food insecurity.

a3947.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAids Executive Director
a3947.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3947.title: UNAids Executive Director
a3947.speech: Warned that US funding cuts will lead to an additional 2,000 new HIV infections each day and over six million further deaths over the next four years ; said the US government’s decision to pause foreign aid – which included funding for HIV programmes – was already having devastating consequences ; called on the US to reverse the cuts immediately, warning women and girls were being hit particularly hard ; said she feared a return to the 1990s, when HIV medication was scarcely available in poorer countries, and infections and deaths soared.

a3947.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAids Executive Director
a3947.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3947.title: UNAids Executive Director
a3947.speech: Thanked Washington for its generosity and humanity, adding it was “reasonable” for the US “to want to reduce its funding - over time”, but said the “sudden withdrawal of lifesaving support [was] having a devastating impact”.

a3947.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAids Executive Director
a3947.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3947.title: UNAids Executive Director
a3947.speech: Speaking in Geneva on Monday, described the case of Juliana, a young woman in Kenya living with HIV who worked for a US-funded programme that supported new mothers to access treatment so their babies did not develop the disease; said that with the programme suspended Juliana was not only out of work but, because she was still breastfeeding her youngest child, she also feared losing the treatment she needed.

a3947.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAids Executive Director
a3947.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3947.title: UNAids Executive Director
a3947.speech: Proposed a deal to the Trump administration, offering an opportunity to market a new US-developed ARV, lenacapavir made by US company Gilead, to millions of people, with UNAids believing 10 million people could benefit from it; added that the profits and jobs resulting from such a deal would be hugely beneficial to the US.

a3947.speaker: UNAids
a3947.name: UNAids
a3947.speech: Has had no indication that other countries might step in to fill the gap left by the US.

a3947.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3947.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3947.speech: Previously said eight countries - Nigeria, Kenya, Lesotho, South Sudan, Burkina Faso, Mali, Haiti and Ukraine - could soon run out of HIV drugs after the US funding pause.

a3947.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief
a3947.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a3947.title: WHO chief
a3947.speech: Warned that disruption to HIV programmes “could undo 20 years of progress”.

a3947.speaker: Treatment Action Campaign (TAC), South Africa’s leading Aids lobby group
a3947.name: Treatment Action Campaign (TAC)
a3947.title: South Africa’s leading Aids lobby group
a3947.speech: In February warned the country could see a return to when HIV patients struggled to access necessary services for their treatment.

a3947.speaker: Sibongile Tshabalala, TAC chair
a3947.name: Sibongile Tshabalala
a3947.title: TAC chair
a3947.speech: “We can’t afford to die, we can’t afford to go back to those years where we were suffering with access to services, especially for people living with HIV treatment.”

a3947.speaker: UN Refugee Agency
a3947.name: UN Refugee Agency
a3947.speech: Has suggested it may have to lose 6,000 jobs.

a3947.speaker: Unicef
a3947.name: Unicef
a3947.speech: Has warned that progress to reduce child mortality is threatened.

a3994.speaker: United Nations (statement)
a3994.name: United Nations (statement)
a3994.speech: Strongly condemned a horrific attack on a market in the Khartoum suburb of Omdurman on February 1st, which resulted in the deaths of at least 60 people and left over 150 injured ; expressed deep concern over reports of civilian killings in other parts of Sudan, including North Kordofan and Darfur, stating that these acts of violence constitute grave violations of international humanitarian and human rights law.

a3994.speaker: Clementine Nkweta-Salami, UN Humanitarian Coordinator for Sudan
a3994.name: Clementine Nkweta-Salami
a3994.title: UN Humanitarian Coordinator for Sudan
a3994.speech: Described the attack, believed to have been carried out by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in an area controlled by the Sudanese army, as “horrific” and “indiscriminate” ; stressed the urgent need for accountability for those responsible for these heinous crimes and reiterated the call for an immediate end to all attacks deliberately targeting civilian areas ; “The suffering of Sudanese civilians has gone on for too long,” she said, emphasizing the urgent need to end the conflict and prevent further devastation.

a3994.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3994.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3994.speech: Has expressed hope that 2025 will mark an end to this bloody conflict.

a3994.speaker: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a3994.name: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a3994.title: WHO Director-General
a3994.speech: “I visited Sudan in September, where I witnessed the devastating effects of the civil war and met people who are paying a heavy price. The following week, I visited the border town of Adre in Chad, where I met some of the 900,000 Sudanese refugees who have fled in search of safety and food.”

a4068.speaker: Senegalese Ministry of Finance and Budget (statement/communiqué)
a4068.name: Senegalese Ministry of Finance and Budget (statement/communiqué)
a4068.speech: Said the 2024 Annual Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank in Washington, held from 21 to 26 October, enabled Senegal to strengthen the confidence of its international partners and to present its new public policy framework; a large Senegalese delegation was "led by the Minister of Finance and Budget, Cheikh DIBA," and included "the Minister of the Economy, Planning and Cooperation, the Minister of Trade and Industry, the Minister of Energy, Petroleum and Mines, the Minister, Secretary General of the Government, and the National Director of the BCEAO for Senegal."

a4068.speaker: Senegalese Ministry of Finance and Budget (statement/communiqué)
a4068.name: Senegalese Ministry of Finance and Budget (statement/communiqué)
a4068.speech: Stressed that, in a context marked by "the publication of the provisional results of the audit of public finances," "this audit was welcomed by the community of partners" and allowed the delegation to "give reassurance about the credible and realistic corrective measures envisaged."

a4068.speaker: Senegalese Ministry of Finance and Budget (statement/communiqué)
a4068.name: Senegalese Ministry of Finance and Budget (statement/communiqué)
a4068.speech: Presented the "new public policy framework which sets out a 'Vision 2050' for a sovereign, just and prosperous Senegal," indicating the vision is "built on four (04) pillars with, as its overall objective, the promotion of endogenous and sustainable development driven by empowered territories."

a4068.speaker: Senegalese Ministry of Finance and Budget (statement/communiqué)
a4068.name: Senegalese Ministry of Finance and Budget (statement/communiqué)
a4068.speech: Noted that "important and strategic meetings were held," citing "the US Treasury Department, the State Department and the US-DFC; the French Treasury, the World Bank, the IMF, the subsidiaries of the IsDB Group, Afreximbank and other technical and financial partners"; discussions with the World Bank focused on "economic reforms, digitalisation and the improvement of economic competitiveness," and at the African Caucus "African priorities such as access to energy and the financing of intra-African trade" were addressed.

a4068.speaker: American authorities (as reported in the Senegalese Finance Ministry statement)
a4068.name: American authorities (as reported in the Senegalese Finance Ministry statement)
a4068.speech: "Welcomed Senegal's approach to transparency," "offering their support to accompany this economic transition."

a4068.speaker: Financial market institutions (as reported in the Senegalese Finance Ministry statement)
a4068.name: Financial market institutions (as reported in the Senegalese Finance Ministry statement)
a4068.speech: "Expressed their support for Senegal for its efforts at transparency in the management of public finances and renewed their interest in mobilising resources in 2024-2025."

a4068.speaker: Senegalese Ministry of Finance and Budget (statement/communiqué)
a4068.name: Senegalese Ministry of Finance and Budget (statement/communiqué)
a4068.speech: Concluded by stressing that "this effort at transparency, recognised and hailed as an act of courage, has strengthened the support of partners who now encourage Senegal to identify and implement concrete and credible reforms."

a4109.speaker: Dr. Rommy Mom, Lawyers Alert
a4109.name: Dr. Rommy Mom
a4109.title: Lawyers Alert
a4109.speech: said there was an urgent need to address gender disparities in healthcare access, particularly for Tuberculosis (TB), HIV, and Malaria in Akwa Ibom State.

a4109.speaker: Dr. Rommy Mom, Lawyers Alert
a4109.name: Dr. Rommy Mom
a4109.title: Lawyers Alert
a4109.speech: Stressing the urgency of local intervention, said, “With USAID’s withdrawal from funding key interventions, local governments and stakeholders must step in to sustain life-saving services, especially for vulnerable women and children.”

a4109.speaker: Situational analysis report conducted under the Gender Equality Fund (GEF) Project
a4109.name: Situational analysis report conducted under the Gender Equality Fund (GEF) Project
a4109.speech: According to findings from the situational analysis, Akwa Ibom State has one of Nigeria’s highest HIV prevalence rates at 5.5%, accounting for 12% of the country’s TB cases, while malaria remains a leading cause of illness and death, particularly among pregnant women and children under five ; the report listed systemic barriers hindering access to healthcare for women to include economic dependency, stigma, and the burden of caregiving responsibilities ; “Many women are unable to seek medical care due to financial constraints, while cultural and religious beliefs often drive reliance on traditional remedies over modern healthcare. The situation is further worsened by frequent stock-outs of TB medications, inadequate diagnostic tools, and poor healthcare infrastructure, particularly in rural areas. The absence of gender-sensitive policies has also led to fragmented interventions, limiting their overall impact on women’s health,” the report stated.

a4109.speaker: Lawyers Alert and Media Health and Rights Initiative of Nigeria (MHR)
a4109.name: Lawyers Alert and Media Health and Rights Initiative of Nigeria (MHR)
a4109.speech: called on the Akwa Ibom State Government, healthcare providers, civil society organizations, and international partners to integrate TB, HIV, and Malaria services into a single, comprehensive framework to enhance resource utilization and ensure holistic care. They also called on the State government to make provision for economic empowerment programs for women to reduce financial dependency and improve healthcare access, strengthening women-led advocacy groups to challenge stigma and push for gender-sensitive health policies ; Other recommendations include increased collaboration with the private sector to mitigate funding shortages and improve the supply of essential medications and diagnostic tools.

a4109.speaker: The NGOs (Lawyers Alert and MHR)
a4109.name: The NGOs (Lawyers Alert and MHR)
a4109.speech: further made case for policy enforcement in addressing healthcare gaps: “We need to strengthen the visibility and enforcement of existing health policies that address gender disparities and stigma reduction. Without this, we cannot achieve meaningful progress.”

a4282.speaker: Albert Chalamila, Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a4282.name: Albert Chalamila
a4282.title: Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a4282.speech: Told mothers who could not afford the cost of gloves to give birth at home, and claimed that he had been a teacher, so he knows how to use examples to make his argument stick; in his story, a mother was told to go home, she and her husband, to look for scissors to deliver the baby after failing to buy gloves as required at the hospital.

a4282.speaker: Albert Chalamila, Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a4282.name: Albert Chalamila
a4282.title: Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a4282.speech: His defence is that these things are expensive - "as our regional commissioner said in his story, these things are expensive."

a4282.speaker: One organisation (unnamed, statement)
a4282.name: One organisation (unnamed
a4282.title: statement)
a4282.speech: Issued a statement condemning that humiliation.

a4282.speaker: Junior official from the Ministry of Health ("mheshimiwa mdogo wa afya")
a4282.name: Junior official from the Ministry of Health ("mheshimiwa mdogo wa afya")
a4282.speech: Claimed that a person contributes a million shillings at a wedding but fails to pay fifty thousand for his wife to give birth - thereby admitting that citizens are in fact required to pay this fifty thousand.

a4282.speaker: TAMASHA (the author's former organisation, motto)
a4282.name: TAMASHA (the author's former organisation
a4282.title: motto)
a4282.speech: "If you want it, Budget" - if you want something, set a budget to make it happen.

a4430.speaker: Dr. Afyare Elmi, authority on global security (article for the Middle East Council on Global Affairs)
a4430.name: Dr. Afyare Elmi
a4430.title: authority on global security (article for the Middle East Council on Global Affairs)
a4430.speech: Recently underscored the fragile state of the Federal Government of Somalia – going so far as to question whether the FGS can survive at all.

a4430.speaker: Military sources
a4430.name: Military sources
a4430.speech: According to military sources, Aadan Yabaal was the largest army base and logistical hub outside the capital, and its capture came with little to no resistance.

a4430.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a4430.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a4430.title: President of Somalia
a4430.speech: On Eid Day (March 30, 2025) called for an inclusive national consultative meeting (Gogol) involving federal member states and other key political stakeholders ; describes his proposed electoral model as a “one-person, one-vote” system.

a4628.speaker: Former USAID official and a health official in Kenya
a4628.name: Former USAID official and a health official in Kenya
a4628.speech: Said that without U.S. funding, distribution from the warehouse, which stocks all U.S. government-donated HIV medicine to Kenya, has ceased, leaving supplies of some drugs worryingly low.

a4628.speaker: Alice Okwirry, 50-year-old HIV patient in Nairobi
a4628.name: Alice Okwirry
a4628.title: 50-year-old HIV patient in Nairobi
a4628.speech: “I was just seeing death now coming,” said Okwirry, who was diagnosed with HIV in 2008 and has a 15-year-old daughter, Chichi, who is also HIV-positive ; “I told Chichi: what about if you hear the drugs are doomed?” Okwirry said, growing emotional. “She told me: Mom, I'll be leaning on you.”

a4628.speaker: State Department
a4628.name: State Department
a4628.speech: Issued a waiver last month exempting funding for HIV treatment from the freeze.

a4628.speaker: Mackenzie Knowles-Coursin, former deputy head of communications for USAID, East Africa, who resigned on Feb. 3 in protest at the dismantling of the agency
a4628.name: Mackenzie Knowles-Coursin
a4628.title: former deputy head of communications for USAID, East Africa, who resigned on Feb. 3 in protest at the dismantling of the agency
a4628.speech: Said the USAID payments system in Kenya is down after the cuts, meaning contractors who implement the programmes cannot be paid: “Projects are left wondering: 'Well, how am I going to resume activities if you're not paying me money?' The waivers that have been given are really waivers on paper.” ; added that in Kenya, officials in Washington have not authorised the release of money required to distribute the $34 million worth of medicine and equipment at the warehouse.

a4628.speaker: Kenyan government document seen by Reuters
a4628.name: Kenyan government document seen by Reuters
a4628.speech: According to the document, about $10 million is needed for that distribution.

a4628.speaker: Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (website)
a4628.name: Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (website)
a4628.speech: Its website says the Christian charity that runs the warehouse supplies drugs to some 2,000 clinics nationwide.

a4628.speaker: USAID
a4628.name: USAID
a4628.speech: Referred a request for comment to the State Department.

a4628.speaker: State Department (non-response)
a4628.name: State Department (non-response)
a4628.speech: Did not respond to a request for comment.

a4628.speaker: Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (non-response)
a4628.name: Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (non-response)
a4628.speech: Did not respond to requests for comment.

a4628.speaker: Deborah Barasa, Kenya's Health Minister
a4628.name: Deborah Barasa
a4628.title: Kenya's Health Minister
a4628.speech: Said she expected her government to mobilise funds to allow the supplies at MEDS to be released within two to four weeks: “We have identified the resources that are required,” she said in an interview.

a4628.speaker: World Health Organization data
a4628.name: World Health Organization data
a4628.speech: According to WHO data, Kenya has the seventh-largest number of people living with HIV in the world, at around 1.4 million.

a4628.speaker: Health official in Kenya (anonymous)
a4628.name: Health official in Kenya (anonymous)
a4628.speech: Said stocks of two critical HIV treatments, Dolutegravir and Nevirapine, were low but did not know exactly how much remained nationwide.

a4628.speaker: Deborah Barasa, Kenya's Health Minister
a4628.name: Deborah Barasa
a4628.title: Kenya's Health Minister
a4628.speech: Said there would be enough Dolutegravir to last five months and Nevirapine to last eight months once the MEDS stocks were released.

a4628.speaker: Nelson Otwoma, director of the National Empowerment Network of People Living with HIV/AIDS in Kenya
a4628.name: Nelson Otwoma
a4628.title: director of the National Empowerment Network of People Living with HIV/AIDS in Kenya
a4628.speech: Said that for the time being, some patients can only get refills of their ARVs for one week at a time.

a4628.speaker: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
a4628.name: Marco Rubio
a4628.title: Secretary of State
a4628.speech: Said on Monday that the Trump administration has cancelled more than 80% of all USAID programmes.

a4628.speaker: Kenyan government's council on syndemic diseases (internal brief seen by Reuters)
a4628.name: Kenyan government's council on syndemic diseases (internal brief seen by Reuters)
a4628.speech: Estimated last month that the U.S. cuts had created funding gaps of around $80 million.

a4628.speaker: John Mbadi, Finance Minister of Kenya
a4628.name: John Mbadi
a4628.title: Finance Minister of Kenya
a4628.speech: Told senators last week that the government was reviewing whether to allocate emergency funding to compensate for U.S. aid cuts before it delivers the 2025/26 budget in the coming months.

a4635.speaker: Finnish government
a4635.name: Finnish government
a4635.speech: Has announced a contribution of 500,000 Euros (572,000 US dollars) to provide tens of thousands of children with daily hot meals as part of Mozambique's School Feeding Programme (PRONAE).

a4635.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP) (press release)
a4635.name: UN World Food Programme (WFP) (press release)
a4635.speech: "This initiative, which will be immediately rolled out, reinforces the shared commitment of the Government of Mozambique, WFP, and partners to improve education, nutrition, and food security in some of the most vulnerable areas of the country" ; says the Finnish contribution "will enable WFP to provide daily hot meals to more than 56,000 students over the next three months in primary schools located along the Nacala Corridor" in the northern province of Nampula ; adds that "evidence shows that school feeding programmes not only improve children's nutrition and learning but also help reduce poverty and inequality by increasing school attendance and building human capital over time".

a4635.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP) (press release)
a4635.name: UN World Food Programme (WFP) (press release)
a4635.speech: Says Mozambique "is currently facing one of the most severe food insecurity crises in recent years, with nearly 40 per cent of children under the age of five suffering from stunted growth and a record 5 million people in need of urgent humanitarian assistance. The situation is especially dire in the northern region, where conflict and recurrent climate shocks continue to disrupt lives and livelihoods".

a4635.speaker: Satu Lassila, Finnish ambassador
a4635.name: Satu Lassila
a4635.title: Finnish ambassador
a4635.speech: "School meals are more than just a plate of food; they are a vital investment in the future of Mozambican children. Finland has a long-standing partnership with Mozambique, including in education. I am delighted that we can now support Mozambican children also in this way."

a4635.speaker: Antonella D'Aprile, WFP Country Director in Mozambique
a4635.name: Antonella D'Aprile
a4635.title: WFP Country Director in Mozambique
a4635.speech: "Investing in school meals is one of the smartest and most impactful ways to support the next generations in Mozambique. Thanks to Finland's generous contribution, thousands of children will receive the nourishment they need to learn and build a better future - not only for themselves but for the country as a whole."

a4679.speaker: Vera Kamtukule, PhD, Malawi Minister of Tourism
a4679.name: Vera Kamtukule
a4679.title: PhD, Malawi Minister of Tourism
a4679.speech: In her public lecture titled ‘Solidifying the gains: Everything. Everyone’ delivered in partnership with Mzuzu University, mentioned failure to coordinate marketing of tourism as the biggest challenge hampering the growth of the industry in the country.

a4679.speaker: Mzuzu University (Mzuni) research, conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Tourism
a4679.name: Mzuzu University (Mzuni) research
a4679.title: conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Tourism
a4679.speech: Cited by the Minister of Tourism as identifying failure to coordinate marketing of tourism as the biggest challenge hampering growth of the industry.

a4679.speaker: Stakeholders in the tourism industry (2025 Malawi International Tourism Expo)
a4679.name: Stakeholders in the tourism industry (2025 Malawi International Tourism Expo)
a4679.speech: Urged the Ministry of Tourism to exploit technology and target global tourism power houses to amplify the three-day initiative to achieve its marketing objective.

a4679.speaker: Ernie Lindsey, American novelist
a4679.name: Ernie Lindsey
a4679.title: American novelist
a4679.speech: “Numbers don’t lie, people do” (quotation widely attributed to him).

a4679.speaker: World Tourism Council data
a4679.name: World Tourism Council data
a4679.speech: Data showing revenues that Malawi and her neighbours generated in 2023 from international tourist visits: Zimbabwe reaped $215.1 million, Zambia generated $901 million and Mozambique raked in $327 million, while Malawi had a paltry $35.5 million; by 2028 Malawi’s tourism earnings are projected to rise to around $268 million, and in 2024 Malawi was projected to earn $42.9 million, a 20.7 percent jump.

a4679.speaker: Malawi 2063 (MW2063) long-term development strategy
a4679.name: Malawi 2063 (MW2063) long-term development strategy
a4679.speech: Identifies tourism as a crucial sector for national economic growth, making it one of the anchors of the urbanisation pillar.

a4910.speaker: Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA)
a4910.name: Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique (CTA)
a4910.speech: Challenges the government to adopt measures to make the business environment more functional and competitive, explaining that this will allow small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to benefit from the opportunities opened by cumulation under the Economic Partnership Agreement between SADC and the European Union ; advocates training companies on the rules of the mechanism, reducing export costs and time through digitalisation, guaranteeing competitive financing and creating industrial zones linked to regional logistics.

a4910.speaker: Onório Manuel, Vice-President of the CTA
a4910.name: Onório Manuel
a4910.title: Vice-President of the CTA
a4910.speech: Speaking during the National Workshop on Cumulation Promotes Trade at FACIM in Maputo, explained that cumulation represents “a bridge” allowing Mozambican products to incorporate inputs from the region and still keep preferential access to the European market, and that this opens space for national SMEs to integrate into regional and global value chains, turning exporting into a process accessible to many and not only to large companies. “An SME in Nampula can buy packaging from Zimbabwe, process its product locally and sell it in Germany free of tariffs. A textile company in Matola can use cotton processed in Malawi and win over the French market” ; warned that cumulation “is not a magic wand”, stressing that the country needs aligned public policies, a bureaucracy that makes life easier for entrepreneurs and a tax system that stimulates business growth ; “The time has come for Mozambique to stop being merely a supplier of raw materials and to become an exporter of value,” adding that the CTA will continue to work alongside the business community to open markets, break down barriers and boost trade.

a4962.speaker: International Cospas-Sarsat Organisation
a4962.name: International Cospas-Sarsat Organisation
a4962.speech: Announced during its virtual session on 13 June the creation of an international working group specialising in artificial intelligence applications in search and rescue satellite systems.

a4962.speaker: National Guard Command / National Search and Rescue Centre (working paper)
a4962.name: National Guard Command / National Search and Rescue Centre (working paper)
a4962.speech: Submitted a working paper during the sessions of the International Committee, attended by representatives from 45 countries and international organisations, on which the decision to give the UAE the chairmanship is based.

a4962.speaker: United Arab Emirates (technical proposal)
a4962.name: United Arab Emirates (technical proposal)
a4962.speech: Put forward a groundbreaking technical proposal aimed at integrating artificial intelligence technologies into the operation of Mission Control Centres (MCC), increasing the efficiency of space-based rescue systems and improving the speed and accuracy of the response to distress calls through intelligent data processing and integration across satellite networks.

a4962.speaker: Cospas-Sarsat member states
a4962.name: Cospas-Sarsat member states
a4962.speech: Gave the UAE's initiative a great deal of praise for its innovation and its forward-looking approach.

a4962.speaker: International Committee for Artificial Intelligence in Search and Rescue Systems
a4962.name: International Committee for Artificial Intelligence in Search and Rescue Systems
a4962.speech: Praised the role of the UAE, its qualitative contribution and its proactive initiatives in deploying modern technologies in support of international humanitarian rescue objectives; adopted the recommendation to form a joint working group chaired by the UAE to coordinate technical cooperation between member states and the competent authorities and to develop artificial intelligence tools linked to mission control centres.

a4964.speaker: Parliamentary Cluster Committee on Health (report on the proposed 2025/26 National Budget)
a4964.name: Parliamentary Cluster Committee on Health (report on the proposed 2025/26 National Budget)
a4964.speech: Urged Treasury this week to cover a K75 billion drug funding gap for the Ministry of Health; in its report following scrutiny of the proposed 2025/26 National Budget, the committee observed that despite the health sector funding increasing this year, it is concerned with the 55 percent deficit in the drugs budget.

a4964.speaker: Mathews Ngwale, chairperson of the Parliamentary Cluster Committee on Health
a4964.name: Mathews Ngwale
a4964.title: chairperson of the Parliamentary Cluster Committee on Health
a4964.speech: Said in an interview that the Ministry of Health's quantification of the medicines and laboratory items for the 2025/26 financial year is K138 billion, but government has allocated just K63 billion, leaving a deficit of K75 billion; he said besides the drug allocation shortfall, central and districts hospitals currently owe Central Medical Stores Trust (CMST) about K11 billion and K30 billion, respectively: "DHOs [district health offices] should receive adequate drug budgets to avoid incapacitating the operations of CMST and government must settle the accrued arrears to allow CMST to [re-capitalise] on its supplies."

a4964.speaker: Mathews Ngwale, chairperson of the Parliamentary Cluster Committee on Health
a4964.name: Mathews Ngwale
a4964.title: chairperson of the Parliamentary Cluster Committee on Health
a4964.speech: Observed that the recent withdrawal of United States Agency for International Development's (USAid) support to Malawi and the threat of other donors following suit, should jolt government to seriously strategise on funding for the health sector, as the aid cuts will affect the availability of drugs and other health services.

a4964.speaker: Mathews Ngwale, chairperson of the Parliamentary Cluster Committee on Health
a4964.name: Mathews Ngwale
a4964.title: chairperson of the Parliamentary Cluster Committee on Health
a4964.speech: Called for additional health financing mechanisms such as compulsory civil servants health insurance, introduction of fees in public hospitals and health levies on various items such as alcohol and tollgates, among others: "You see, instead of introducing compulsory health insurance for civil servants, the government actually asked who wants to go on health insurance. Only 12 percent of civil servants said yes, therefore, we are still where we were. We cannot depend on the budget alone. We cannot depend on the money that MRA [Malawi Revenue Authority] collects to fund the health sector, it will not work."

a4964.speaker: Government's National Health Financing Strategy (2023-2030)
a4964.name: Government's National Health Financing Strategy (2023-2030)
a4964.speech: Says as much, stressing that the only way to stretch any macro-fiscal space to accommodate extra spending on healthcare is to implement a radical reconfiguration of sectoral shares of the budget in favour of health.

a4964.speaker: USAid termination note of March 3 2025
a4964.name: USAid termination note of March 3 2025
a4964.speech: Information in the note indicates that just one area of HIV and Aids has lost $163 521 653 (about K283.5 billion) in Malawi.

a4964.speaker: United Kingdom government
a4964.name: United Kingdom government
a4964.speech: Early this month announced that it would cut its foreign aid from 0.5 percent of gross national product to 0.3 percent to free up money for defence spending amid growing threats from Russia and collapsing security guarantees from the US.

a4964.speaker: Abuja Declaration on Health (adopted by the African Union, April 2001)
a4964.name: Abuja Declaration on Health (adopted by the African Union
a4964.title: April 2001)
a4964.speech: Stipulates that African countries who are signatories to the pact should allocate 15 percent of the total budget to the health sector to improve healthcare access.

a4964.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a4964.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a4964.speech: According to WHO, general government expenditure for Malawi hovering around 23 percent of gross domestic product places Malawi as a low to medium level of fiscal capacity.

a4964.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a4964.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a4964.speech: Recommends a health sector investment of at least $80 (about K140 080) per capita.

a4964.speaker: Malawi Health Sector Strategic Plan III (HSSPIII), 2023-2030
a4964.name: Malawi Health Sector Strategic Plan III (HSSPIII)
a4964.speech: Found the $80 per capita unattainable, and set the target of $50 (about K87 500) per capita by 2030.

a4964.speaker: Maziko Matemba, executive director of the Health and Rights Education Programme
a4964.name: Maziko Matemba
a4964.title: executive director of the Health and Rights Education Programme
a4964.speech: Said in an interview that the budget for medicines should cover at least half of the health sector investment budget; pointed out that funding for medicines should be a priority in any national budget: "Most Malawians are unable to buy medicines on their own. This might result in preventable deaths from serious health cases; hence, the need to address the issue of funding" ; urged MPs to push for increased allocation towards the drug budget, and for government to consider alternative health financing mechanisms, especially now that development partners are pulling out funding.

a4964.speaker: Maziko Matemba, executive director of the Health and Rights Education Programme
a4964.name: Maziko Matemba
a4964.title: executive director of the Health and Rights Education Programme
a4964.speech: Observed: "The United States aid freeze will create huge gaps in health sector services. The country needs to plan ahead so that it does not experience drug stock outs in the event that other donors do not come in to boost drug stocks."

a5079.speaker: James Knight, Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin
a5079.name: James Knight
a5079.title: Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin
a5079.speech: In his speech at the launch ceremony, stated that enormous challenges persist despite the considerable efforts made over the past ten years in the fight against malaria ; gives assurance: "the United States of America reaffirms its commitment to work alongside the Beninese government in the success of the various relevant initiatives taken within the framework of this fight."

a5079.speaker: Dorothe Kinde Gazard, Minister of Health of Benin
a5079.name: Dorothe Kinde Gazard
a5079.title: Minister of Health of Benin
a5079.speech: Said the Beninese government is more than ever committed alongside international partners so that the fight against malaria becomes a reality in Benin.

a5217.speaker: FBC Securities Private Limited (stockbroker), in a statement titled “US Foreign Aid Halt: Impact on Zimbabwe’s Economy”
a5217.name: FBC Securities Private Limited (stockbroker)
a5217.title: in a statement titled “US Foreign Aid Halt: Impact on Zimbabwe’s Economy”
a5217.speech: has urged the government to strengthen domestic revenue mobilization, improve investor confidence and restructure state-owned enterprises (SOEs) in view of an expected reduction in external financial support, and urged immediate government action to mitigate potential destabilization of critical economic and social sectors: “To mitigate these challenges, the Zimbabwean Government must take decisive action by strengthening domestic revenue mobilization, restoring investor confidence and restructuring state-owned enterprises (SOEs)” ; “These strategies are deemed essential for navigating the challenges posed by declining external support and ensuring long-term economic resilience.”

a5217.speaker: FBC Securities Private Limited (stockbroker)
a5217.name: FBC Securities Private Limited (stockbroker)
a5217.speech: suggested that Zimbabwe seeks alternative funding from other international donors, regional partners, and non-traditional allies, including the African Union and Southern African Development Community (SADC); said such partnerships could provide crucial financial and technical assistance, replacing the withdrawn US support.

a5217.speaker: FBC Securities Private Limited (stockbroker)
a5217.name: FBC Securities Private Limited (stockbroker)
a5217.speech: reported that NGOs contributed significantly to foreign currency liquidity, accounting for 10% and 9% of total foreign currency receipts in the first nine months of 2023 and 2024, respectively; warned that a reduction in these cash inflows would lower disposable incomes and consumer spending, particularly impacting vulnerable communities in rural areas; predicted a decline in bank deposits in Foreign Currency Accounts, foreign currency inflows in general, diminished stock market liquidity, and increased volatility in blue-chip stocks because of the US action.

a5217.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5217.name: Donald Trump
a5217.title: US President
a5217.speech: announced the country’s withdrawal from the World Health Organisation (WHO) and the suspension of funding to PEPFAR (President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief).

a5296.speaker: Geological surveys
a5296.name: Geological surveys
a5296.speech: suggest Somalia possesses significant reserves of oil, gas, and precious minerals, such as gold, iron ore, and uranium among others.

a5296.speaker: Key statistics (cited)
a5296.name: Key statistics (cited)
a5296.speech: suggest that agriculture contributes 19.7% to GDP (or 65% when combined with livestock); livestock alone accounts for over 40% of GDP and 50%+ of export earnings; the livelihood of over 70% of the population depends on these sectors.

a5296.speaker: Wardheernews.com (2025)
a5296.name: Wardheernews.com (2025)
a5296.speech: according to it, Somalia imports roughly 50 tonnes of Kenyan Miraa every day. In 2023, with prices at around $23 per kilogram, this meant a daily spend of about $1.1 million - totalling nearly $420 million a year. With Kenya now doubling its prices, Somalia's annual outlay could soar to almost $1 billion.

a5328.speaker: Bandiougou Dante, President of the Maison de la Presse
a5328.name: Bandiougou Dante
a5328.title: President of the Maison de la Presse
a5328.speech: Announced the launch of a series of capacity-building activities for media professionals on the occasion of the electoral contests; explained that this requires a necessary complementarity, without leaving out partner support or accompaniment.

a5328.speaker: Rachna Korhonen, Ambassador of the United States to Mali
a5328.name: Rachna Korhonen
a5328.title: Ambassador of the United States to Mali
a5328.speech: Said media and information literacy is not only a tool for journalists but a powerful weapon for every citizen wishing to understand the world and contribute actively to building a more just and equitable society; in her view, quality information is the cornerstone of democracy.

a5328.speaker: Mohamed Ag Abachar, Chief of Staff of the Ministry of Communication, the Digital Economy and the Modernisation of the Administration
a5328.name: Mohamed Ag Abachar
a5328.title: Chief of Staff of the Ministry of Communication, the Digital Economy and the Modernisation of the Administration
a5328.speech: Paid tribute to those who lost their lives on the field of honour; stressed that the training workshops would be held in Sikasso, Bamako and Segou respectively, launched within the dynamic framework of a partnership between the Maison de la Presse and the USA through their embassy; said that for the promotion of peace and national unity, media professionals are invited to be vanguard actors.

a5328.speaker: Sadou Yattara and Mahamane Hameye Cisse, trainers
a5328.name: Sadou Yattara and Mahamane Hameye Cisse
a5328.title: trainers
a5328.speech: Explained the regulation of communication and the media, the stakeholders and actors in elections, journalistic ethics and professional conduct, and reporting during the electoral period; codes and charters raised included the code of ethics of the Malian journalist, the broadcasting charter for radio and television, the code of good conduct, the bloggers' charter, the Appel Mali charter, the charter of expression of the network of women of Mali, the charter for the protection of children and the charter for the inclusion of vulnerable persons.

a5328.speaker: Participants in the training session
a5328.name: Participants in the training session
a5328.speech: At the end of the session, formulated recommendations addressed to the strategic partner and to the Maison de la Presse, with a view to strengthening the professionalism of journalists.

a5591.speaker: Top executive at Kikkoman (unnamed)
a5591.name: Top executive at Kikkoman (unnamed)
a5591.speech: "Ah yes; our soya sauce dispenser, that was one of my first projects with the company, working with the designer, Kenji Ekuan."

a5591.speaker: Kenji Ekuan, industrial designer
a5591.name: Kenji Ekuan
a5591.title: industrial designer
a5591.speech: Told an interviewer about the early post-war years after witnessing the destruction of Hiroshima: "Faced with that nothingness, I felt a great nostalgia for human culture. I needed something to touch, to look at. Right then I decided to be a maker of things." ; in a brochure prepared for an exhibition of his designs he described his reactions to the bombing of his city, writing that he heard the voices of street cars, bicycles and other objects mangled and abandoned, saying they had wished to have been utilised more.

a5591.speaker: Kenji Ekuan, industrial designer
a5591.name: Kenji Ekuan
a5591.title: industrial designer
a5591.speech: Wrote in a serialised memoir of his life in a leading Japanese newspaper: "The path of Buddha is the path to salvation for all living things, but I realised that, for me, the path to salvation lay in objects. Objects have their own world. Making an object means imbuing it with its own spirit." ; insisted that the images of the destroyed family-owned Buddhist painting of heaven and hell remained in his mind as "one of my design ideals".

a5591.speaker: Kenji Ekuan, industrial designer
a5591.name: Kenji Ekuan
a5591.title: industrial designer
a5591.speech: Said he always maintained that his inspiration for the soya sauce bottle was a memory of his mother awkwardly pouring soya sauce from a large storage container into a smaller container for the table.

a5591.speaker: Kenji Ekuan, industrial designer
a5591.name: Kenji Ekuan
a5591.title: industrial designer
a5591.speech: Insisted he was never a fan of mindless futurism: "When we think of the evolution of design, we might imagine a world where robots are everywhere, but that's not it, the ultimate design is little different from the natural world."

a5591.speaker: Kenji Ekuan, industrial designer
a5591.name: Kenji Ekuan
a5591.title: industrial designer
a5591.speech: Wrote in The Aesthetics of the Japanese Lunchbox: "There can be no doubt that the sensitivities of people from other countries who have chosen Japanese products are tuned into the frequencies that broadcast the beauty and quality we here in Japan produce. The lunchbox spirit is something that can be understood and absorbed by people the world over. When I see those in other countries buying, enjoying, and using all manner of Japanese goods, I am ever more convinced that everyone posses tuning bands broad enough to receive this signal of quality."

a5591.speaker: Amazon.com review of The Aesthetics of the Japanese Lunchbox
a5591.name: Amazon.com review of The Aesthetics of the Japanese Lunchbox
a5591.speech: "Ekuan reads the Japanese lunchbox as both object and metaphor. It is one of this book's many charms that he is able to see it as both simultaneously. He compares the visual pleasures of the Zen lunchbox to an aerial view of the Japanese archipelago; he invites us to savor its quadripartite structure as we savor the four seasons. In so doing, he unlocks the secrets of ancient Japanese rituals, celebrates the aesthetics of Japanese design, explores the contours of Japanese landscapes and technology.... With an agility more characteristic of poetry than of design criticism, he connects everything from food, television, motorcycles, package tours, and department stores to landscape, ecology, computers, and radios, all the while keeping his eye on his subject."

a5591.speaker: Kikkoman (company figures)
a5591.name: Kikkoman (company figures)
a5591.speech: The company figures it has now sold over 300 million of these little bottles.

a5606.speaker: Somalia (government position at international forums)
a5606.name: Somalia (government position at international forums)
