a5606.speech: has voiced consistent support for Ukraine’s territorial integrity at international forums.

a5971.speaker: Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of Mozambique
a5971.name: Daniel Francisco Chapo
a5971.title: President of Mozambique
a5971.speech: Urged the consolidation of a renewed partnership between Mozambique and Japan, focused on the development of the Nacala Corridor and the exploitation of liquefied natural gas from the Rovuma Basin ; emphasized that the conference's motto, "Co-creating Innovative Solutions with Africa", is a call for a new era of partnership based on the joint transformation of challenges into opportunities for mutual gains ; recalled that the Yokohama meeting also serves to evaluate the implementation of the commitments made at TICAD-8, held in 2022 in Tunis, and to strengthen the alignment between the African Union's Agenda 2063 and the United Nations' Agenda 2030.

a5971.speaker: Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of Mozambique
a5971.name: Daniel Francisco Chapo
a5971.title: President of Mozambique
a5971.speech: Explained that the government's 2025-2029 Five-Year Program prioritizes the integrated development of infrastructure along development corridors: "One of our strategic actions is to promote integrated development and infrastructure along national and regional development corridors, especially the Nacala Corridor, where we count on Japan as a strategic partner" ; noted that investment in roads, bridges, railways, ports, airports, and digitalization processes is crucial to boosting free trade in the Southern African Development Community (SADC) and strengthening connectivity with the world ; "Allow me to highlight the Nacala Development Corridor, recognized by the TICAD platform itself as a privileged gateway for Japanese investment in Southern Africa" ; demonstrated that the Nacala Corridor plays a central role in regional integration, connecting Mozambique to Malawi, Zambia, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and added that the government is resuming the economic development strategy for this axis, which "has enormous potential" for sustainable agriculture and the stimulation of regional trade ; expressed confidence that the Nacala Corridor will boost the economies in the SADC region by improving infrastructure and transportation services for people and goods in their respective markets, and expressed appreciation to Japan for its commitment to supporting the development of this strategic axis.

a5971.speaker: Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of Mozambique
a5971.name: Daniel Francisco Chapo
a5971.title: President of Mozambique
a5971.speech: Highlighted mineral and energy resources as another priority in the relationship with Japan, with an emphasis on liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the Rovuma Basin: "I would like to conclude by highlighting investment in mineral resources and energy as another priority, with an emphasis on liquefied natural gas (LNG) in Area 1 of the Rovuma Basin, in Cab Delgado" ; said this is a structural project, not only for Mozambique but also for the entire region, and is considered fundamental for the country's rapid industrialization and the consolidation of a regional energy connectivity corridor.

a6048.speaker: US Embassy in Pretoria
a6048.name: US Embassy in Pretoria
a6048.speech: Declined to discuss Gaspard's pending nomination to the Pretoria position.

a6048.speaker: The Washington Post
a6048.name: The Washington Post
a6048.speech: According to The Washington Post, Gaspard also was involved in union-based anti-Apartheid efforts during the 1980s.

a6048.speaker: The Washington Post
a6048.name: The Washington Post
a6048.speech: Appraising his background and experience, described him by saying, “Gaspard is a thoroughly liberal Democrat. He has consistently supported liberal candidates and has worked closely with labour unions throughout his career.”

a6048.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, Executive Director of the Democratic National Committee
a6048.name: Patrick Gaspard
a6048.title: Executive Director of the Democratic National Committee
a6048.speech: Asked in 2006 what his goal was for 2008, he said, “That's the easiest question I've ever been asked – I want to begin to repair the imbalance in the Supreme Court by electing a Democratic president.”

a6048.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, Executive Director of the Democratic National Committee
a6048.name: Patrick Gaspard
a6048.title: Executive Director of the Democratic National Committee
a6048.speech: When the US Supreme Court upheld “Obamacare” in its landmark decision, triumphantly tweeted about the decision, “It's constitutional, Bitches.”

a6156.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the US Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a6156.name: Elon Musk
a6156.title: head of the US Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a6156.speech: Stated that the process of dismantling the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) was under way. "We are going to shut it down," Musk said in a broadcast on his social network X ; According to Elon Musk, the agency should not be restored. "It has become obvious that this is not an apple with a worm in it," he said. "What we have is just a ball of worms. All of it has to be got rid of. It is beyond repair," he added.

a6156.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the US Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a6156.name: Elon Musk
a6156.title: head of the US Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a6156.speech: Earlier, Musk had accused USAID of funding the development of biological weapons.

a6156.speaker: The Associated Press
a6156.name: The Associated Press
a6156.speech: Cited sources according to which two USAID security officials were placed on administrative leave because of a conflict with DOGE. They refused to hand over classified documents to Elon Musk's agency.

a6156.speaker: NBC News
a6156.name: NBC News
a6156.speech: At the end of January, NBC News reported that more than 50 USAID employees had been placed on administrative leave with full pay and benefits until further notice.

a6156.speaker: Jason Gray, new acting administrator of USAID
a6156.name: Jason Gray
a6156.title: new acting administrator of USAID
a6156.speech: The decision was taken following an audit that revealed "several actions within USAID that appear to be intended to circumvent presidential executive orders and the mandate of the American people," according to the agency's new acting administrator, Jason Gray.

a6389.speaker: Anderson Miamen, Executive Director of the Center for Transparency and Accountability in Liberia (CENTAL)
a6389.name: Anderson Miamen
a6389.title: Executive Director of the Center for Transparency and Accountability in Liberia (CENTAL)
a6389.speech: Highlighted the project's primary goals, which include increasing citizen demand for accountability, fostering public engagement in managing natural resources, and empowering citizen voices ; “This project seeks to empower citizens by fostering active dialogue between the government and local communities,” Miamen noted. “We aim to strengthen participation in decision-making processes, particularly through the oversight of revenue sharing laws, ensuring equitable resource distribution.”

a6389.speaker: Eddie Jarwolo, Executive Director of Naymote Partners for Democratic Development
a6389.name: Eddie Jarwolo
a6389.title: Executive Director of Naymote Partners for Democratic Development
a6389.speech: Stressed the significance of localizing governance efforts. “Localization is taking root globally, from Sweden to Ireland, and we're eager to strengthen the capacity of local institutions here in Liberia,” Jarwolo said, acknowledging the collaboration with stakeholders like the Ministry of Internal Affairs and media representatives.

a6389.speaker: Gerard Considine, Irish Ambassador
a6389.name: Gerard Considine
a6389.title: Irish Ambassador
a6389.speech: Praised the project, noting that accountable institutions and robust governance are essential for sustainable progress. “Institutions grounded in strong governance and adherence to the rule of law are vital for achieving transformative development that benefits those furthest behind,” said Ambassador Considine, who also announced a strategic 2024-2028 plan to reinforce political and economic cooperation in Liberia.

a6389.speaker: Gerard Considine, Irish Ambassador
a6389.name: Gerard Considine
a6389.title: Irish Ambassador
a6389.speech: Emphasized that the initiative would focus on key areas, including gender equality, food security, climate action, and governance enhancement ; also acknowledged the role of the European Union and other national integrity institutions in these efforts, stating, “Ireland recognizes the importance of partnering with civil society to strengthen accountability in governance.”

a6389.speaker: Gerard Considine, Irish Ambassador
a6389.name: Gerard Considine
a6389.title: Irish Ambassador
a6389.speech: Expressed optimism for the involvement of various government agencies, highlighting how inclusive governance can drive equitable resource distribution and improved public services for all Liberians ; called for unity in advancing Liberia's development objectives, especially in alignment with the government's draft development strategy, Arrest for Inclusive Development. “We look forward to working together to achieve our shared goals of transparent and accountable leadership,” he said, reaffirming Ireland's commitment to Liberia's progress.

a6477.speaker: Diplomats and aid officials
a6477.name: Diplomats and aid officials
a6477.speech: Said the termination of aid had jeopardised counterterrorism efforts and weakened US influence in a part of the world where some countries had turned to Russian mercenaries for help.

a6477.speaker: Yacouba Doumbia, 78-year-old chief of Kimbirila-Nord
a6477.name: Yacouba Doumbia
a6477.title: 78-year-old chief of Kimbirila-Nord
a6477.speech: “What attracts young people to extremists is poverty and hunger.” ; “There was a very dangerous moment in 2020. The project came at the right time, and allowed us to protect ourselves.”

a6477.speaker: This year’s congressional report on implementation of the Global Fragility Act
a6477.name: This year’s congressional report on implementation of the Global Fragility Act
a6477.speech: The US goal in this area was to “seize a narrowing prevention window,” according to the report.

a6673.speaker: Monica Chakwera, First Lady of Malawi and TB ambassador for Malawi and SADC
a6673.name: Monica Chakwera
a6673.title: First Lady of Malawi and TB ambassador for Malawi and SADC
a6673.speech: While addressing the gathering, she emphasised the urgent need for sustainable local funding for TB prevention and treatment services: "Collectively, we need to act with urgency and commitment, investing in resources that can help end TB by 2030. This will require the private sector and other stakeholders to mobilise funds domestically."

a6673.speaker: Monica Chakwera, First Lady of Malawi and TB ambassador for Malawi and SADC
a6673.name: Monica Chakwera
a6673.title: First Lady of Malawi and TB ambassador for Malawi and SADC
a6673.speech: Underscored the need for a stronger multi-stakeholder approach to continue fighting TB; said Malawi should not, at any cost, lose the recent gains made in the fight against the disease, warning that any slippage would be a painful blow to the country as a whole ; highlighted the progress made by Malawi under the Leprosy and Tuberculosis Programme, including the integration of HIV and Aids treatment with TB services, which she said has been crucial: "Reduced mortality rates, which are currently at 54 percent among HIV-negative people and 60 percent among HIV-positive people, as well as high treatment success rates, are signs that we are doing well in the fight against TB. We need to intensify efforts to completely end the disease" ; said the fight is far from over and requires concerted efforts from various sectors to eliminate the disease's burden, and observed that the fight against TB cannot be won by the health sector alone.

a6673.speaker: Noah Chimpeni, Deputy Minister of Health of Malawi
a6673.name: Noah Chimpeni
a6673.title: Deputy Minister of Health of Malawi
a6673.speech: Said the ministry is working on increasing domestic resource mobilisation as a way of addressing the heavy reliance on external funding, which accounts for 64 percent of the total health expenditure: "The emphasis on self-reliance is key to the long-term sustainability of healthcare. As such, there is a need to improve efficiency in healthcare spending and examine areas, including costly referrals outside Malawi."

a6673.speaker: Edna Tembo, executive director of the Coalition of Women Living with HIV in Malawi
a6673.name: Edna Tembo
a6673.title: executive director of the Coalition of Women Living with HIV in Malawi
a6673.speech: Has said the recent suspension of US foreign aid will significantly impact efforts to fight TB and other diseases, and called on the government and the private sector to respond collectively to the changes, which have caused a major setback.

a6673.speaker: Kuzani Mbendera, Deputy Programme Manager for the Malawi National TB and Leprosy Elimination Programme
a6673.name: Kuzani Mbendera
a6673.title: Deputy Programme Manager for the Malawi National TB and Leprosy Elimination Programme
a6673.speech: Indicated that Malawi continues to make great strides, with the treatment success rate for TB standing at 90 percent on average, as of September 2024.

a6680.speaker: Report titled "Botswana Food & Beverages Imports (for January 2025)" (official data)
a6680.name: Report titled "Botswana Food & Beverages Imports (for January 2025)" (official data)
a6680.speech: Revealed that Botswana imported food and beverages worth nearly P1 billion in January 2025, representing 16.4 percent of the country's total imports of P6.6 billion for the month; that Beverages, Spirits & Vinegar, along with Cereals, led the Food and Beverages import categories, accounting for 20.2 percent and 17.1 percent respectively, followed by Sugars and Sugar confectionery at 9.3 percent; "Beverages, Spirits and Vinegar was the most prominent commodity imported," the report noted; that Beer Made From Malt was the single largest beverage imported at 37 percent of that category, other fermented drinks including cider, mead and sake 24.3 percent, and Sweetened and Flavored Waters including Aerated Soft Drinks 16.2 percent; and that "Other Maize (Corn)" dominated Cereal imports at 44.9 percent, with Grain Sorghum following at 23.9 percent.

a6804.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (press release)
a6804.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (press release)
a6804.speech: Announced it has selected Liberia as newly eligible to develop a compact, in recognition of the country's commitment to pursuing critical economic and democratic governance reforms; said MCC expects all partner countries to continue demonstrating an ongoing commitment to the principles of inclusive democratic governance that underpin MCC's eligibility criteria; stated that eligibility does not guarantee that Liberia will receive a compact program and that MCC and the U.S. Embassy look forward to working closely with the Government of Liberia to launch the compact development process, with the size and content of the final program contingent on analytical work, the availability of funds, and the MCC Board of Directors' approval.

a6804.speaker: Alice Albright, MCC Chief Executive Officer
a6804.name: Alice Albright
a6804.title: MCC Chief Executive Officer
a6804.speech: “MCC is proud of our longstanding history with Liberia and is enthusiastic about embarking on a new partnership to advance opportunities for the people of Liberia.”

a6831.speaker: Liberia Electricity Corporation
a6831.name: Liberia Electricity Corporation
a6831.speech: Announced a sharp reduction following the decision of its Ivorian supplier to cut its supply by 85% (from 50 MW to 7.5 MW).

a6831.speaker: JoyNews (Ghanaian media outlet)
a6831.name: JoyNews (Ghanaian media outlet)
a6831.speech: According to JoyNews, the Ghanaian government on average received $150 million in funding from USAID, and in 2025 it intends to obtain $137.7 million from the American organisation for education, medicine, agriculture and other sectors of the economy.

a6831.speaker: Niger’s leadership (military authorities)
a6831.name: Niger’s leadership (military authorities)
a6831.speech: Ordered the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to leave the country without giving an official reason.

a6865.speaker: Human Development Report 2023/2024, United Nations Development Programme
a6865.name: Human Development Report 2023/2024
a6865.title: United Nations Development Programme
a6865.speech: reveals that African countries have the lowest Human Development Index (HDI) score. Out of the 52 African countries ranked in the HDI, only four made it into the top 100. ; The report indicates that the continent's strong economic growth has not necessarily translated into improved global rankings.

a6869.speaker: Trump administration (court filing)
a6869.name: Trump administration (court filing)
a6869.speech: said in a court filing late on Tuesday night that it “cannot” meet a federal judge's 23:59 Wednesday deadline for releasing frozen funds to foreign aid contractors and grant recipients ; asked the appeals court to put Judge Ali's order on hold so it could consider the appeal.

a6869.speaker: Pete Marocco, acting deputy administrator of the US Agency for International Development and director of foreign assistance at the State Department (declaration)
a6869.name: Pete Marocco
a6869.title: acting deputy administrator of the US Agency for International Development and director of foreign assistance at the State Department (declaration)
a6869.speech: saying the required payments would take “multiple weeks” ; Marocco's declaration states the delay is due primarily to new processes put in place by the Trump administration to ensure that payments are legitimate and comply with the administration's policy goals ; Marocco said that the total amount of payments required by Ali's order was close to $2 billion.

a6869.speaker: Amir Ali, US District Judge
a6869.name: Amir Ali
a6869.title: US District Judge
a6869.speech: had already ruled that those were not valid grounds to delay payments.

a6869.speaker: Plaintiffs (USAID and State Department contractors and grant recipients)
a6869.name: Plaintiffs (USAID and State Department contractors and grant recipients)
a6869.speech: argue that Trump has violated federal law and the US Constitution by largely dismantling USAID, which Congress established as an independent agency in 1998.

a6985.speaker: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA/ECA)
a6985.name: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA/ECA)
a6985.speech: Said on Tuesday that much still needs to be done for Africa to increase internet penetration as the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the continent's trade and socioeconomic condition.

a6985.speaker: UN Economic Commission for Africa (ECA figures)
a6985.name: UN Economic Commission for Africa (ECA figures)
a6985.speech: According to figures from the ECA, Kenya, Mauritius, Namibia and South Africa are the only countries where the share of online shoppers exceeds 8 percent, while the trend is below 5 percent in “most other countries” in Africa.

a6985.speaker: Mama Keita, director of ECA's Eastern Africa region
a6985.name: Mama Keita
a6985.title: director of ECA's Eastern Africa region
a6985.speech: “The COVID-19 pandemic changed the way we do business, and this should be an accelerator for digital transformation. Sectors like education, health, trade, food delivery, events and conferencing experienced unprecedented demand for technology.”

a6985.speaker: Mama Keita, director of ECA's Eastern Africa region
a6985.name: Mama Keita
a6985.title: director of ECA's Eastern Africa region
a6985.speech: Stressed that Africa's projected GDP growth of 3.2 percent for 2020 is now expected to be a sharp contraction ; emphasized how the COVID-19 crisis and containment measures have upended almost every aspect of life, affecting big and small enterprises, disrupting supply chains, causing the decline of export revenues and interrupting the tourism, transport and logistics sectors significantly ; noted that East Africa's economic growth, although highly impacted too, is expected to remain the largest in Africa ; “COVID-19 pandemic should be used as a game-changer. It should serve as a wakeup call underscoring the urgency to turn Africa's structural vulnerabilities into opportunities.”

a6985.speaker: Mama Keita, director of ECA's Eastern Africa region
a6985.name: Mama Keita
a6985.title: director of ECA's Eastern Africa region
a6985.speech: Said that the over reliance on imports from the rest of the world of essential goods such as medical, pharmaceutical and food items should be reduced considerably and gradually be replaced with local production.

a6985.speaker: International Telecommunication Union (ITU) figures
a6985.name: International Telecommunication Union (ITU) figures
a6985.speech: Recent figures from the ITU showed that only 28 percent of Africans used the internet in 2019, while online shoppers are relatively still few in the continent.

a6985.speaker: Experts attending the virtual dialogue
a6985.name: Experts attending the virtual dialogue
a6985.speech: Stressed that in the wake of COVID-19, there is an urgent need for African enterprises to digitalize and tap into enormous opportunities offered by e-commerce.

a6985.speaker: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a6985.name: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a6985.speech: Said that as of Tuesday, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases across the African continent reached 736,288 while the number of deaths related to the pandemic rose to 15,418 ; said 391,898 patients who tested positive for COVID-19 have recovered across the continent.

a7119.speaker: Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama), as espoused by its president Bertha Bangara-Chikadza
a7119.name: Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a7119.title: as espoused by its president Bertha Bangara-Chikadza
a7119.speech: Called for urgent action to achieve fiscal discipline, export-led recovery and reform of foreign exchange markets to avert a deeper balance-of-payments crisis ; said Malawi will require a combination of monetary tightening to curb speculation and long-term investment in export growth to restore macroeconomic stability, cautioning that the widening trade gap is fuelling forex shortages, driving transactions underground and worsening inflationary pressures.

a7119.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) statement
a7119.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) statement
a7119.speech: Showed that Malawi's net international reserves (NIR) were projected to fall to negative $2.03 billion (about K3.55 trillion or 18.9 percent of gross domestic product) by the end of this year; projected that Malawi's net international reserves - or what the Reserve Bank of Malawi can actually use after deducting liabilities - will deteriorate from -$1.02 billion in 2023 to -$2.03 billion in 2025.

a7119.speaker: Bloomberg
a7119.name: Bloomberg
a7119.speech: Reporting that part of Malawi's external debt total includes almost $500 million owed to Africa Export and Import Bank (Afreximbank) and about $400 million with the Trade and Development Bank.

a7119.speaker: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a7119.name: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a7119.speech: Maintained the policy rate at 26 percent in a move some economists described as a 'cautious' approach that takes into account the existing inflation risk, especially on rising maize prices.

a7119.speaker: MacDonald Mafuta-Mwale, Reserve Bank of Malawi Governor
a7119.name: MacDonald Mafuta-Mwale
a7119.title: Reserve Bank of Malawi Governor
a7119.speech: Said in February, barely a month in office, that the central bank had finalised the process of formulating measures aimed at crushing the parallel market foreign exchange supply as a key price stabilisation strategy.

a7141.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) partnership / UN-backed food security assessment
a7141.name: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) partnership / UN-backed food security assessment
a7141.speech: Warned Monday that half of Gazans are experiencing "catastrophic" hunger, with famine projected to hit the north of the territory by May unless there is urgent intervention ; estimated that 1.1 million people - half the population, according to UN data - were facing catastrophic conditions ; said famine in the north of Gaza was "imminent... projected to occur anytime between mid-March and May" ; said that while the technical criteria for famine had not yet been met, "all evidence points towards a major acceleration of deaths and malnutrition" ; "Waiting for a retrospective famine classification before acting is indefensible."

a7141.speaker: Cindy McCain, head of the UN's World Food Programme (WFP)
a7141.name: Cindy McCain
a7141.title: head of the UN's World Food Programme (WFP)
a7141.speech: "People in Gaza are starving to death right now. The speed at which this man-made hunger and malnutrition crisis has ripped through Gaza is terrifying."

a7141.speaker: Beth Bechdol, deputy director general of the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a7141.name: Beth Bechdol
a7141.title: deputy director general of the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a7141.speech: "To have 50 percent of an entire population in catastrophic, near-famine levels, is unprecedented." ; told AFP that Gazans are "turning to alternative sources" for food, including animal feed and "inedible items, purely out of desperation".

a7141.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a7141.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a7141.speech: Said this was the "highest number of people ever recorded as facing catastrophic hunger" under the IPC system, originally developed in 2004 ; according to the WFP, "one in three children below the age of two is now acutely malnourished, or 'wasted'", meaning they are dangerously thin ; said meeting basic food needs would require at least 300 trucks to enter Gaza every day, especially in the north, and that the agency has managed to get only nine convoys into the north since January, the latest on Sunday night involving 18 truckloads of food supplies delivered to Gaza City.

a7141.speaker: Martin Griffiths, the UN's humanitarian chief
a7141.name: Martin Griffiths
a7141.title: the UN's humanitarian chief
a7141.speech: Called for Israel to allow unfettered access for aid to the besieged Palestinian territory, saying there was "no time to lose".

a7141.speaker: Vedant Patel, US State Department spokesperson
a7141.name: Vedant Patel
a7141.title: US State Department spokesperson
a7141.speech: Said the findings were "alarming", and revealed a "heartwrenching" picture of "children who are starving": "That is why we believe so strongly that everything must be done to scale up the delivery of humanitarian assistance."

a7141.speaker: Hiba Tibi, country director for the CARE international aid group
a7141.name: Hiba Tibi
a7141.title: country director for the CARE international aid group
a7141.speech: "Hunger is a slow and painful death," and reported aid workers seeing children "who can barely talk and walk" for lack of food.

a7141.speaker: World Health Organization (statement)
a7141.name: World Health Organization (statement)
a7141.speech: In a statement, pointed to the lasting effects of malnutrition, particularly on children, warning that the "current situation will have long-term effects on the lives and health of thousands".

a7141.speaker: Arif Husain, WFP chief economist
a7141.name: Arif Husain
a7141.title: WFP chief economist
a7141.speech: Said the final criteria for declaring a famine - the mortality rate - could be met within weeks ; "Our hope is we can still avert a full-fledged famine. But the window is shutting and it is shutting very, very fast."

a7141.speaker: UN's Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a7141.name: UN's Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a7141.speech: Said it could be already happening in the north, where data is patchy.

a7141.speaker: UN agencies
a7141.name: UN agencies
a7141.speech: Say that donor deliveries by air or sea are not viable alternatives to land deliveries.

a7141.speaker: Oxfam (aid charity)
a7141.name: Oxfam (aid charity)
a7141.speech: Accused Israel on Monday of continuing to "systematically and deliberately block and undermine" the delivery of aid into Gaza, in violation of international humanitarian law.

a7141.speaker: Israel
a7141.name: Israel
a7141.speech: Has repeatedly defended its procedures for allowing aid into Gaza.

a7141.speaker: COGAT, Israeli defence ministry body governing civilian affairs in the occupied Palestinian territories (statement on X)
a7141.name: COGAT
a7141.title: Israeli defence ministry body governing civilian affairs in the occupied Palestinian territories (statement on X)
a7141.speech: Saying in a statement on X that 222 trucks of supplies had entered on Monday, two-thirds of them carrying food.

a7141.speaker: United Nations (UN data)
a7141.name: United Nations (UN data)
a7141.speech: The UN says there are about 300 000 people in the north of Gaza ; a famine is declared when 20 percent of households face an extreme food shortage - which is the case in Gaza, the UN says.

a7149.speaker: Essa Wally, president of the Association of Customs, Clearing and Forwarding Agencies (ACCFA)
a7149.name: Essa Wally
a7149.title: president of the Association of Customs, Clearing and Forwarding Agencies (ACCFA)
a7149.speech: Disclosed that the Gambia is ranked among the highest in total imports from Ecowas countries, registering a percentage of 12.8%: "Looking at the statistics of the Gambia comparatively the statistics reveals that the highest percentage of total import from the Ecowas bloc is 14% registered by Burkina Faso followed by Gambia with a percentage of 12.8 and Code Ivoire with a percentage of 12.1%." ; added that in terms of export value within the bloc, Gambia registered a percentage of 56.2 followed by Togo with a percentage of 52.4% and Senegal with a percentage of 31.5% ; "The total trade of the region has an average of $208.1 billion. Exports are projected at approximately $137.3 billion while imports total about $80.4 billion. The main active countries in trade are Nigeria, which alone accounts for approximately 76 percent of total trade followed by Ghana (9.2 percent) and Cote d'Ivoire (8.64 percent). The trade surplus of the region, estimated at $47.3 billion is attributable to Nigeria ($58.4 billion) and Cote d'Ivoire ($3.4 billion) when all other Countries have a deficit in the trade balance."

a7149.speaker: Statistics gathered by Ikechi, Chinedum, and Nwokoro (study cited by Essa Wally)
a7149.name: Statistics gathered by Ikechi
a7149.title: Chinedum, and Nwokoro (study cited by Essa Wally)
a7149.speech: According to Wally, the statistics gathered by Ikechi, Chinedum, and Nwokoro provided evidence of the untapped potential in sub-regional trade because of the lack of implementation of regional agreements that were designed to eliminate tariff and non-tariff barriers to trade in the sub-region.

a7149.speaker: Essa Wally, president of the Association of Customs, Clearing and Forwarding Agencies (ACCFA)
a7149.name: Essa Wally
a7149.title: president of the Association of Customs, Clearing and Forwarding Agencies (ACCFA)
a7149.speech: "We are gathered here to talk to ourselves and interrogate the existence of our very regional co-existence as ECOWAS citizens." ; "What exists today in our sub-region in the level of free trade between member states is not something that any of us here present can be proud of. We are now together preparing the next journey of this Organization to the regional level. Our choices will determine what this organization becomes. It is time for each of us to ensure that we take charge of the destiny of our organization and have the same sense of responsibility that we are demanding. All of us present here are coming from an ECOWAS member state and the Alliance of the Sahel state. What we are discussing is to complement ECOWAS efforts and protocols." ; said the objectives of the ECOWAS, AFCFTA, and AES are to prepare customs officials and stakeholders to have an understanding of their protocols, agreements, and implementation guidelines, and stated that their targets are the stakeholders involved in the shipping and transport sector, customs clearing & forwarding agents in the region ; "It is therefore important that we use this meeting to take stock of the challenges confronting the sector in the transportation of goods and the free movement of persons in our sub region."

a7149.speaker: Essa Wally, president of the Association of Customs, Clearing and Forwarding Agencies (ACCFA)
a7149.name: Essa Wally
a7149.title: president of the Association of Customs, Clearing and Forwarding Agencies (ACCFA)
a7149.speech: "This association we are about to reactivate by injecting life into it again will look forward to continue collaborating with the ECOWAS, AFCFTA the AU, and other institutions in our shared mission to strengthen and sustain a thriving trade ecosystem." ; "I am appealing to this august gathering that when this association is reactivated, we should make it a point to engage the ECOWAS, the AU, and any other institution to prioritize the promotion of coastal vessels into our waters. There has been a long conscious effort made to develop and sustain coastal shipping in West and Central Africa."

a7201.speaker: Fraternite Matin (Ivorian newspaper)
a7201.name: Fraternite Matin (Ivorian newspaper)
a7201.speech: Announces the opening of four new toll stations in Cote d'Ivoire.

a7201.speaker: Government of Cote d'Ivoire (statement of Monday 10 February 2025)
a7201.name: Government of Cote d'Ivoire (statement of Monday 10 February 2025)
a7201.speech: Specifies that the new toll stations are the Katiola toll station on the Bouake-Katiola axis, that of Ebouassue on the Abengourou-Bondoukou axis, and the Lakota and Eticoon-Tollakro toll stations on the N'Douci-Divo-Gagnoa axis.

a7201.speaker: Jeune Afrique (magazine)
a7201.name: Jeune Afrique (magazine)
a7201.speech: Reports that Tidjane Thiam will soon be "freed" from his French nationality, and stresses that becoming exclusively Ivorian is a sine qua non condition for being eligible in the presidential election next October.

a7201.speaker: Tidjane Thiam, president of the PDCI
a7201.name: Tidjane Thiam
a7201.title: president of the PDCI
a7201.speech: Announced that he had begun the administrative steps to become exclusively Ivorian, nine months before the Ivorian presidential elections.

a7201.speaker: Financial Afrik (news website)
a7201.name: Financial Afrik (news website)
a7201.speech: Returns to the impact of the halt to USAID funding decided by American President Donald Trump: "Nigeria, Tanzania and Uganda will be the hardest hit by the withdrawal of the main foreign aid of the United States via the American development agency," noting that in 2023 Nigeria received 368 million dollars, followed by Tanzania with 337 million.

a7201.speaker: L'Essor (Malian newspaper)
a7201.name: L'Essor (Malian newspaper)
a7201.speech: Reports the introduction of new taxes by the transitional government as part of a "citizen contribution", with three adopted texts concerning the tax on access to the telecommunications network paid by operators, the tax on alcoholic beverages, and the levy on top-ups and mobile money transactions.

a7201.speaker: Transitional government of Mali
a7201.name: Transitional government of Mali
a7201.speech: Justifies these measures by the need to stabilize the economy, optimize the management of resources and modernize public infrastructure.

a7201.speaker: Le Soleil (Senegalese newspaper)
a7201.name: Le Soleil (Senegalese newspaper)
a7201.speech: Questions the capacity of the health system to cope with epidemics and future threats, after having been shaken by "Ebola, Covid-19 and Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever".

a7201.speaker: Senegalese doctors
a7201.name: Senegalese doctors
a7201.speech: Analyse whether the Senegalese health system is ready to manage a new crisis.

a7201.speaker: EnQuete (Senegalese newspaper)
a7201.name: EnQuete (Senegalese newspaper)
a7201.speech: Points to another difficulty, the exodus of health workers: because of "difficult working conditions, derisory salaries and the lack of infrastructure", many Senegalese doctors prefer to resign in order to work abroad, with France at the top of the destinations thanks to a well-organized recruitment.

a7213.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7213.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7213.title: President of Ghana
a7213.speech: Has instructed Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson to urgently take action to close a significant $156 million funding gap, in response to the recent suspension of aid by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).

a7213.speaker: Statement from the President’s office (Ghana)
a7213.name: Statement from the President’s office (Ghana)
a7213.speech: According to a statement from the President’s office, the decision follows a strategic review of Ghana’s current financial landscape and the challenges posed by the aid freeze.

a7278.speaker: Chakudza Linje, Director of Financial Markets at the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a7278.name: Chakudza Linje
a7278.title: Director of Financial Markets at the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a7278.speech: Has called on the private sector to step up efforts in producing and exporting goods to help the country generate foreign exchange, emphasizing that the Central Bank does not create forex, it only manages it: "For a country to have foreign currency, it must export. As a Central Bank, our role in exports is very limited. The private sector is the engine of economic growth, and we urge businesses to enhance production in sectors that can generate forex to help address the ongoing foreign exchange challenges."

a7278.speaker: Chakudza Linje, Director of Financial Markets at the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a7278.name: Chakudza Linje
a7278.title: Director of Financial Markets at the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a7278.speech: Explained how the 26% policy rate was determined by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).

a7278.speaker: Chakudza Linje, Director of Financial Markets at the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a7278.name: Chakudza Linje
a7278.title: Director of Financial Markets at the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a7278.speech: Expressed optimism about lower inflation by year-end, citing good rains and expected bumper harvests that could drive food prices down, but warned against unfounded inflation speculations, saying they unnecessarily push prices higher: "When there is speculation, there is a reaction, prices go up. Let's be positive and base our discussions on facts."

a7278.speaker: Feston Malekezo, Nyika Media Club Chairperson
a7278.name: Feston Malekezo
a7278.title: Nyika Media Club Chairperson
a7278.speech: Echoed her sentiments, stressing the need for journalists to verify information, especially as elections approach: "Fact-checking is an essential part of journalism. With elections around the corner, there will be a flood of information, and it's our duty to ensure we present credible, truthful, and factual news."

a7458.speaker: Peasant farmers of the Diaca administrative post, Cabo Delgado
a7458.name: Peasant farmers of the Diaca administrative post
a7458.title: Cabo Delgado
a7458.speech: Presented the concern to the Secretary of State in Cabo Delgado Province, Antonio Supeia, that those who returned to Diaca after the restoration of security are not managing to reopen the fields of agricultural production owing to the lack of agricultural inputs and the lack of support.

a7458.speaker: Antonio Supeia, Secretary of State in Cabo Delgado Province
a7458.name: Antonio Supeia
a7458.title: Secretary of State in Cabo Delgado Province
a7458.speech: Did not speak about the chainsaws that the district Government promised to the peasant farmers of Diaca, having only committed himself to mobilising more support for the recovery of agriculture.
